**And Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah: And Enoch walked with God after he begat Methuselah three hundred years, and begat sons and daughters: And all the days of Enoch were three hundred sixty and five years: And Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.*

**Hebrews 11:5**
*By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because God had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.*

**Jude 1:14-15**
*And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.*

I've read that, when we look at these early patriarchs, we can see the pattern for salvation.

Adam knows God, his creator, and knows his sin. Abel brings the blood of atonement, given in faith for redemption. Seth and Enos, that with the mouth, confession is made, calling upon the name of the Lord. And with Enoch, we have the testimony that he walked with God, that he lived separated, pleasing God.

That each of us goes through these steps when we come to Christ and live for Him. An illustration given by God in His word, through the lives of these men.

But what of Enoch? The seventh from Adam (not to be confused with Cain's son, 3rd from Adam), Enoch was a prophet. A preacher, who gave witness in the Spirit to Christ's victory on the day of the Lord.

We know that by faith, he was transformed, translated that he should not see death.

But this is the promise to all saved by faith in Jesus.

**John 8:51**
 *Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.*

So what then? What does scripture mean by saying he was "translated?" That he was not found? Does it mean bodily ascension? Literally taken by God, not just his bodily death?

In **John 3**, Jesus says "*no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven,*" referring to Himself.

What then are we to take from this? Is there a hidden meaning to the story of Enoch? Can we dwell in ancient texts and Jewish fables searching for his fate? Certainly.

Lots of rabbi holes to go down with his story.

But what we can know from scripture is that Enoch walked with God, prophesying of Christ, and was pleasing to God. And draw inspiration to live in accordance to that ourselves, seeking to be similarly pleasing to God. In faith. In the Spirit. Not knowing death.

And that's really all that matters.

teachings.title: How to increase your faith
teachings.summary: Faith grows by hearing the word, doing it, praying for faith, and obeying God in things like church and tithing so that His kept promises teach us to trust Him more.
teachings.text:
How to increase your faith? The Bible tells us:

**Romans 10:17**
*So then faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*

Read the word and listen to preaching from His word.

**James 1:22-24**
*But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.*

By living the word we begin to rely more of God and less on ourselves. The word becomes part of us, shoring up faith.

**Psalm 51:12-14**
*Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; And uphold me with thy free spirit. Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; And sinners shall be converted unto thee. Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, thou God of my salvation: And my tongue shall sing aloud of thy righteousness.*

Pray for faith.

**Malachi 3:10**
*Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.*

God says to prove, or test Him. Obey His word (go to church, pay tithes in this example) and see how His blessings reward your faith in being a doer of the word. God keeping His promises is a huge way to learn to trust Him with more.

teachings.title: Daily bread: prayer and the word against temptation
teachings.summary: A daily walk of prayer and Bible reading feeds the new man and keeps Satan at bay, while neglecting them leaves us without the means of escape God has given.
teachings.text:
It is our daily walk with God that protects us. We ask Him to provide our daily bread, not just physical need for food, but spiritually, studying the word of God. We start our day in prayer, taking to God, and reading His word that His will be made known to us. His promises made clear that we may grow in faith. This is how we resist temptation. This is how we keep Satan at bay.

We are weak in the flesh, but if we feed the spirit, the "new man," as Paul describes it, that quickened spirit that is the surety of our eternal life, we shall overcome as Jesus has overcome.

And when we walk after the flesh, and neglect our prayers and our reading of the word, and we get caught up in the cares of this world, the way Satan caught up Jesus to the top of that mountain, to the heights of the temple, and we fear, and lust, feel wrath, covet and put ourselves at risk tempting God, and have not the means to escape though God has given them to us. His word; The pattern made by Christ to follow.

teachings.title: Beginning each day as the Lord's first fruits
teachings.summary: As the tabernacle was reared on the first day of the first month and the firstfruits belong to God, the believer gives himself to God daily, washed in Christ's blood and sanctified by the Spirit through his walk.
teachings.text:
**Exodus 12:1-2**
*And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying, This month shall be unto you the beginning of months: it shall be the first month of the year to you.*

**Exodus 40:17**
*And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up.*

It has been a year for the children of Israel, a year since the passover and exodus from Egypt. A year in the wilderness, preparing all that God required; the covenant, the Tabernacle, the carnal ordinances and priestly vestments. The diverse washings and oils ready. The veil over the word of God, in the Ark at the heart of the Tabernacle.

And it is fitting on the first day of the first month that it is given to the Lord God as His. The first fruits are His. The first sons of Israel. The first of the flock. The first 10th of your earnings. All His. And as we begin each day as His, seeking first the kingdom of God.

**Luke 9:23**
*And he said to them all, If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.*

**1 Corinthians 15:31**
*I protest by your rejoicing which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord, I die daily.*

We give to God ourselves daily. We put on the new man daily. We renew ourselves while we are yet in the flesh, beginning everything with God if we walk in the spirit.

And on that first day of the first month, Moses washed Aaron and his sons, anointing the vessels and sanctifying all, according to the word of God.

**Leviticus 20:7-8**
*Sanctify yourselves therefore, and be ye holy: for I am the Lord your God. And ye shall keep my statutes, and do them: I am the Lord which sanctify you.*

**John 17:17**
*Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.*

**Hebrews 13:12**
*Wherefore Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered without the gate.*

**Romans 6:6**
*Knowing this, that our old man is crucified with him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin.*

We are washed in His blood, we are sanctified in the Spirit and we are made new daily, by our walk with Christ.

**Philippians 1:6**
*Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ*

teachings.title: Secret sin and the Father's rod
teachings.summary: God chastens His adopted children and brings secret sins to light, and the guilt of conscience should drive the believer to confess and forsake sin.
teachings.text:
Of course, David takes Bathsheba as his wife, one of many. He lives with his sin and the poor decisions he has made. But the Lord is displeased and David's actions won't remain hidden for long.

**Hebrews 12:6-7**
*For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?*

**Hebrews 10:26-27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

That fearful looking for judgment, the guilt we feel when we disobey God's word, the pangs of our conscience, is a powerful motivation to get right with the Lord. To call out to Christ our redeemer for forgiveness, to repent of our actions and seek to do the right thing. Especially knowing that, as adopted children, our Father will not spare the rod, and the sins we do in secret will be revealed in the light.

**Psalms 90:8**
*Thou hast set our iniquities before thee, our secret sins in the light of thy countenance.*

**Proverbs 28:13**
*He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy*.

**Luke 8:17**
*For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.*

teachings.title: Seek ye first the kingdom of God
teachings.summary: Solomon building God's house before his own shows that those who seek God's kingdom first are blessed, not with a prosperity gospel but with fellowship and reward, as pillars in Christ's temple.
teachings.text:
Solomon built the House of God in 7 years, his own palace in 13. His zeal was towards the Lord.

**Matthew 6:33**
*But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

By seeking first the things of God, Solomon had the peace and blessings to them see to his own. The same promise to all believers, that in building up the temple of Christ, of which every believer is a pillar, we will be blessed in our lives.

**Mark 10:28-30**
*Then Peter began to say unto him, Lo, we have left all, and have followed thee. And Jesus answered and said, Verily I say unto you, There is no man that hath left house, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my sake, and the gospel's, But he shall receive an hundredfold now in this time, houses, and brethren, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and lands, with persecutions; and in the world to come eternal life.*

Not a "prosperity gospel," so much as a promise to be rewarded in our relationships with others, and the opening of their homes to those who do the work of the Lord. Fishers of men. Persecution and all, but we shall overcome.

**Revelation 3:12**
*Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.*

The pillars Hiram made for the Temple, named *Jachin*—He will establish; and *Boaz*—in Him is strength, pictures of that Heavenly temple in which we are pillars of Christ's church.

teachings.title: Wisdom maketh his face to shine
teachings.summary: Walking with God and being anointed by the Spirit changes a believer's countenance and gives boldness to preach the truth, so that others see they have been with Jesus.
teachings.text:
The Preacher continues his sermon. Having said he has searched for wisdom by observation of all things under the Sun, and having found all have sinned and fallen short. That the wise and the fool, the rich and the poor, all are appointed to die, and after this, judged and found wanting, that then the only way is God's. That fear of Him and seeking His favor is the only alternative to the vanity and vexation of spirit that man travails in.

Solomon begins **Ecclesiastes 8** praising the effect that seeking God's wisdom has on us. That it makes the face to shine, and to speak boldly His truth. That it changes the countenance of a person to walk with God.

**Exodus 34:29-30**
*And it came to pass, when Moses came down from mount Sinai with the two tables of testimony in Moses' hand, when he came down from the mount, that Moses wist not that the skin of his face shone while he talked with him. And when Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, behold, the skin of his face shone; and they were afraid to come nigh him.*

Moses had to cover his face from the people, it disturbed them so much to see the radiance coming from his time with God.

**Psalm 104:15**
*And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, and oil to make his face to shine, and bread which strengtheneth man's heart*.

The Spirit is described as oil, which anoints us as we walk in Him. The bread, His word. Our heart, merry from the juice of the vine, which is Christ. He does make our faces shine. His light magnified through us, that men see us and know, we have been with Jesus. And the boldness of our wisdom comes from the confidence we have in Him and His word.

The Spirit filled the disciples of Christ, gathered in the upper room on Pentecost, and having His anointing, they went out among the multitudes gathered for the feast in Jerusalem, and preached with boldness.

Acts 2:1-4
*And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance*.

The men, hearing the miracle of preaching Christ from scripture, in their own tongues, languages from around the known world, they wondered; *Behold, are not all these which speak Galilaeans?* But the disciples had been changed by their time with God. The boldness to preach Christ from scripture, and 3,000 souls came to repentance.

Just as when Peter and John were brought before the religious leaders of the Jews for preaching Christ, these lowly fishermen gave witness that they had been with Christ by their boldness.

**Acts 4:13**
*Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.*

Their light so shined, that others saw and praised God. The anointing of the Spirit, the truth of God's word, the wisdom they trusted, gave them boldness to preach the truth. They were changed.

The understanding that man's countenance gives away their time with God to others, has a counterpoint in scripture. That the reprobate, those that hold the truth in unrighteousness, have a similar change;

**Isaiah 3:9**
*The shew of their countenance doth witness against them; and they declare their sin as Sodom, they hide it not. Woe unto their soul! for they have rewarded evil unto themselves.*

We should seek to walk with God, to be anointed with the Spirit, that men look upon us and take note that we have been with Jesus. To speak boldly the wisdom of the gospel. To make known the truth of His way.

teachings.title: The bride who would not open
teachings.summary: The bride who delayed to open to her beloved pictures saved believers who grow complacent and make excuses when God calls them to His work, and so lose His fellowship and suffer His chastening.
teachings.text:
Chapter 5 opens with the aftermath of the close of the previous chapter, which ended with the woman calling upon her bridegroom, her lord.

The spiritual moment of acceptance and humility, asking Him for salvation. Opening yourself to be intimately known of God.

Verse 1 gives the bridegroom's POV. Having entered the garden, come unto his dearest sister, his spouse, gathered the spices and ointments of myrrh, eaten the sweet of the honeycomb, drunk the wine and milk, and calling those at the wedding feast, and his bride, to eat and drink, abundantly.

**Revelation 22:17**
*And the Spirit and the bride say, Come. And let him that heareth say, Come. And let him that is athirst come. And whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely.*

This picture of salvation, the immediate joy and celebration, the call to get your fill of an abundance of the sweet and precious food and anointing oils, wine and milk, to drink abundantly, is God's call to us to now walk in His Spirit. To take full advantage of the relationship His children have with the Father in Christ, the true King. The Shepherd. The Bridegroom. Not a thief, but our Savior.

**John 10:10**
*The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.*

We are called to walk in the Spirit and receive the fruit thereof;

**Galatians 5:22–25**
*But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law. And they that are Christ’s have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts. If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.*

This initial feeling of having come to a feast and being overwhelmed with the love of God towards us, His blessings and rest, is marvelous. But we may tire and sleep in that contentment.

The bride sleeps, but her heart wakes. She hears a knock. A voice. It is her beloved, calling to her to let him in. He asks her to open to him, *my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled*. He has come, his hair wet with the dew of the night to see her.

He is Christ come to give His bride a blessing, but she doesn't leap to open the door.

She makes excuses; *I have put off my coat; how shall I put it on? I have washed my feet; how shall I defile them?* Rather than hear His voice and do His will, that we may be blessed, a believer may see their contentment and undefiled spirit as a bed to rest upon. When God asks so little of us whom He has saved, to open when He knocks, will we respond?

**Revelation 3:20**
*Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.*

In the Christian life, God gives us works to do. Poor to be fed. A gospel to be preached. Divine appointments to be kept. His burden is light. He wants so little from us, yet in our own selfish interests, we make excuses. Taking for granted all He has given us.

And, even as the beloved reaches his hand in through the door, making that extra effort to stir his bride, God will try and overcome our hesitation, moving in our lives.

His effort stirs her. She rises but too late. She feels the sweet smelling myrrh, the holiness of Christ, upon the lock. But, He has withdrawn.

When we don't respond to God's callings, and hesitate to do His will, He will give us a taste of life without Him. He will lift His hedge of protection. He will let us suffer consequences He has spared us from. He will chasten every son.

The bride's soul fails, knowing she did wrong and desperately she seeks her beloved, in the very manner she once sought him. Wandering in the dark streets, calling for him. Trying to find her own way.

This time, the watchmen find her and persecute her. The smote her and wound her and remove her veil of purity. She suffers for her love's sake.

The watchmen who could not tell her the way to her love in chapter 3, now treat her wickedly.

teachings.title: I am my beloved's
teachings.summary: The bride's choice to rise early and go forth with her beloved pictures the mature believer deliberately making Christ the centre of each day and working with Him to bear fruit in new believers.
teachings.text:
Song of Solomon 7 opens with the King, having called his beloved Shulamite woman to return to him that he may look upon her at the end of chapter 6, now detailing what he sees of his beloved. He describes her beauty and the perfect symmetry of her body.

*How fair and how pleasant art thou, O love, for delights!*

Everything he sees of her is good. Just as we are seen as perfect and without spot when God looks upon us, clothed in the righteousness of Christ.

**2 Corinthians 11:2**
*For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.*

**Colossians 1:22**
*In the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and unblameable and unreproveable in his sight*

**Jude 1:24–25**
*Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen.*

The woman responds to her husband, her brother, her spouse with unwavering confidence;

*I am my beloved’s, and his desire is toward me.*

We are Christ's, and His desire is for us.

Beginning there in verse 10, she responds to her beloved, knowing she is his, and inviting him to go forth with her, to live with her. To get up early to the vineyards, to see the vine flourish and come to fruition, where she will give him her love.

The spiritual application here; She has gone from her initial humble acceptance of his love, to the joy of the wedding feast, to her period of complacency, persecution, profession of faith and renewal, to now making the decision to plan her day and life around him, is a beautiful picture of the Christian life.

A believer makes the conscious decision to make Jesus their companion. To go forth with Him and to reside with Him. To wake early in the morning, starting the day with Christ, and His word. In prayer.

This intentionality is contrasted with the bride laying in bed, hesitant to wake, making excuses to avoid letting in her beloved. As mature Christians, in it for the long haul, we seek Him first.

We work with Him to tend the vine, which is His church, bringing forth fruit which are new believers. Planting the seed of His word. Watering and nurturing. Tending to them, the babes in Christ, and helping them grow to maturity. Through it all, giving Him all our love.

We lay up our fruit, those people we have given the gospel to, the needy to whom we give comfort. The broken hearted we have consoled. This treasure we have laid up for Heaven, but to Him is the increase. We give Him our all because He is our beloved.

teachings.title: No want to them that fear Him
teachings.summary: God provides for those who fear Him and live righteously, chastens those who do not, and expects believers to love the brethren by not forsaking the assembling of the local church.
teachings.text:
*O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.*

Believers, sanctified in the Spirit by faith in the risen Christ, are given the promise that the Lord will redeem us, His servants.

But His provision for us extends beyond the fact of eternal salvation, and gives us hope and comfort here, in this life. Our daily bread, shelter, clothing, we shall not want for any good thing.

But more, He's given us His word, and His standards for separation that we may fear the Lord and be blessed by having a longer life and see good within the years we are allotted.

His burden is light. Don't speak evil of others, don't lie. Don't seek to harm others, but do good and seek peace.

**Romans 12:18**
*If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.*

Vengeance is Mine, sayeth the Lord. He will repay. We not only believe He is, and a rewarder of those that diligently seek Him, but that He is our shield and strength against our enemies. We do not need to fight a battle, but trust in Him to fight for us. We simply need to walk in the Spirit, love our enemies, hate His, and seek others' profit. Doing good.

If we want our Father's blessing, live righteously. He hears the righteous and answers their cry.

We are known by our love for the brethren. By our edifying one another.

**Hebrews 10:22–25**
*Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water. Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;) And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.*

You don't want the face of God against you in your time of need.

**Hebrews 10:26–29**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries. He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?*

God will chasten His children. He will shorten your life and withhold blessings, and even bring you home for not doing His work at His pleasure.

**Hebrews 10:31**
*It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.*

Note that we are expected to love and care for our fellow saints. And where do we do this? On the called out assembly of believers. Our local church. Forsaking this opportunity is spiteful to the Spirit of grace which has bought you. Go to church!

teachings.title: Rites and ordinances become a religion unto themselves
teachings.summary: Like the Pharisees, churches that put their weight on rites, washings and sacraments lose the spiritual meaning and slide into tying salvation to ritual, when sin and salvation are matters of the heart.
teachings.text:
One of the problems with replacing the spiritual application of biblical principles and examples with rites and ceremony, carnal ordinances and diverse washings, and dietary laws and restrictions, is that, as the Bible demonstrates, these sacramental ordinances become a religion unto themselves. Just as the Old Testament which was a symbol of the Christ to come, eventually devolved into the phariseitical religion practiced in Jesus day, Christian churches who put all their emphasis in these vain traditions of men, the pomp and circumstance, lose the spiritual aspect of what it represents. And in doing so run the risk of running into a damnable heresy where their ability to perform a ritual or the frequency with which they do is tied directly into their salvation.

The lesson of God's word should be for us to understand the spiritual nature of our eternal lives rather than the limited and short nature of our corruptible flesh.

All things in creation point to the spiritual lessons and are there for our edification and learning. All ritual and levitical practices were there to point us to the spiritual meaning. Meats for the belly and belly's for the meats, but our spirit and what is in our hearts is what we take with us when our flesh dies. That's where our sin is. And that's where our salvation is in the quickening of our inner man.

As Jesus said it's not what goes into the mouth that defiles a man, but what comes out of it. A man who's committed adultery in his heart, feels hatred to another, has sinned just as much as those who commit the act.

It's why Jesus spoke in parables because there are those among us who cannot live in the spirit, but only in the flesh and so they cannot receive the things of God.

teachings.title: Alms, prayer and fasting in secret, and take no thought
teachings.summary: Jesus condemns public religious show, vain repetitions and treasure on earth, which he likens to the Catholic church, and teaches us to seek God's kingdom first and not worry, since worry is worship of the god of this world.
teachings.text:
The sermon of Jesus Christ on the mount continues. I rather think this is representative of Jesus preaching during His earthly ministry, and many themes here are repeated in the other Gospels to showcase and teach us His perfect and flawless doctrine.

Give alms in secret to men, for our Father will reward you. Pray in secret, not making a show of it, and the Father who knows all our needs before we do will openly reward you. Don't pray as the heathen do, with vain repetitions thinking they will be heard for much speaking. Don't place your heart on treasures in this world, material wealth, but rather treasure what you may lay up in Heaven. Don't make a public show of fasting and doing without. Don't even let anyone know that you are fasting.

Essentially, don't act like the Catholic Church.

Jesus says that they who pray and give alms in public to fanfare, who fast, abstaining from meats, giving up treats, to be seen as holy to men, those who pray with novenas and roseries, repeating the same words again and again, a vain prayer of repetition, those who place their treasure on earth, serving mammon, materialists with gilded shrines and golden fixtures, ornate buildings full of idols...all these get their reward, Christ assures us. And it isn't a blessing but a curse.

No man can serve two masters, as scripture says. You can't serve an earthly, fleshly, material god of this world, and serve the Father. *He will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other.*

And so Jesus tells us that worry for materialism, for vain glory, for grudges held, debt unforgiven, the accumulation of things, this is serving Mammon. Not God. Not seeking the Kingdom of Heaven. Eyes full of darkness.

Worry is a prayer to the god of this world. Fear is the worship of him.

But we are children of the light and are looking forward to a better country, establishing the works thereof. Storing up the crowns and precious stones of heavenly rewards. Keeping our eyes turned to Heaven.

Taking no thought for what we wear, shelter, food. Trusting God to provide for our needs as He does for His creation throughout nature. Living faith to faith. Unafraid.

*Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.*

*Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.*

Don't worry about tomorrow, if the Lord blesses us with a tomorrow, He will provide. The evil of today is sufficient enough without adding cares for things yet to come. But keep in faith. He will provide.

teachings.title: Corban and what truly defiles a man
teachings.summary: Jesus exposed the Pharisees' Corban loophole as breaking God's law to honour parents and taught that defilement comes from the heart, not unwashed hands, food or ordinances.
teachings.text:
The Gospels are full of these confrontations by Jews accusing Jesus. Here we see their religious leaders saying Jesus' disciples had violated the law by not washings their hands before eating, but it was law by tradition of man, not from God. Jesus turns the tables on them, questioning their allowing of sons to abandon care for their parents by declaring their wealth "Corban," a gift to God, one that allowed them to continue use of the wealth, even releasing it from being a 'gift' but never providing for their parents. **Mark 7:11** has this parallel passage;

*But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.*

This loophole violates God's law to honor our father and mother, with the obligation to care for them in their old age. If a parent came to a child, seeking relief, and the child went to the Pharisees declaring their extra wealth as reserved for God, rather than being put to death for dishonoring then, he would be exempt and they would go without.

There is a popular idea that the Pharisees we're hyper-legalists, having an unyielding adherence to the law, but in truth these hypocrites we're just like the Talmudic Judasism of today; constantly justifying breaking of God's law to please themselves. Hypocrites and vipers.

Jesus, having rebuked them, preaches an important understanding of doctrine; that the things of the flesh, what goes into our mouth, which ends up in the drought, or toilet, is not what defiles us. Rather, what is in our hearts, and what we speak (because out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks). The flesh profits nothing. Meats for the belly, and belly for the meats. Over and over again the Bible tells us that it is with our heart and mind and tongue that we sin. That it's the thought of sin, of foolishness, of lust, wrath and hatred. Our intent. And diverse washings and dietary laws and carnal ordinances of the tradition of men, eating of bread, drinking of wine, circumcision, worship of things made of man from wood, metal and stone...none of these material things save us or make us more spiritual.

Once again, Peter, that is the stone, Cephas, doesn't get it and asks Jesus to explain. We tend to think of Peter as a bit simple but he is often a stand in for us, as we seek wisdom and understanding. Jesus further explains the parable, and then departs for other cities to continue His ministry to the lost sheep of Israel.

A Canaanite woman, full of faith comes begging Jesus to heal her daughter, possessed by a devil, and Jesus first ignores her. She persists to His disciples, and they being bothered ask Jesus to send her away.

He explains again His earthly ministry during His time was to gather them unto repentance, so that they would be first fruits and later spread the truth of the Gospel to all nations, after His resurrection.

She persists, and likening her unto a dog, Jesus says it isn't hers to ask for, but her faith wins out, and she answers Him that even dogs may eat of the crumbs cast off from the masters table. Her faith solid, Jesus shows mercy on her and heals her daughter.

We see in this example and of the multitudes He feeds in the following verses, that persistent faith brings Jesus to have mercy on us. God is moved by compassion when we make an effort to maintain our faith in Him. And when we do, He works miracles in our lives. Regardless of who we are.

teachings.title: Bodily exercise profiteth little
teachings.summary: Every creature is good to eat being sanctified by the word and prayer, and godliness, not the flesh, is what profits, since God is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.
teachings.text:
Now to edify Timothy in his role as evangelist to the Ephesians, Paul gives yet more advice as to the doctrines he should be certain to instruct the churches.

That every creature is good to eat, *For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer*, just as God told Adam and again to Noah. The dietary laws and carnal ordinances given to Moses for a season, done away with in Christ. This understanding will help the men of the church "be a good minister of Jesus Christ," not because of the food they eat, but rather the understanding of prayer and God's blessing. That, as Jesus said, *the flesh profits nothing,* rather they will *be  nourished up in the words of faith and of good doctrine.*

And so, avoid old wives tales, similarly, Jewish fables, and be about exercising godliness, their spirit, not the flesh.

*For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come.*

We the saved, *having*, present tense, the promise of the life that now is and the eternal life that awaits, must exercise and grow, spiritually. Godliness is our gainz, for our eternal life will be built upon that, not our PRs at the gym.

*This is a faithful saying and worthy of all acceptation.*

And therefore, because of this doctrine of faith, living Godly, in the spiritual rather than the flesh, the *faithful sayings* Paul writes unto Timothy, he warns they will both labor to teach others, and be rebuked by those of this world, *because we trust in the living God, who is the Saviour of all men, specially of those that believe.*

(Note to calvinists, God is the savior of all men, specially those who believe. Christ died for everyone, especially to those who believe and are saved)

teachings.title: The sabbath was made for man
teachings.summary: Jesus taught that the sabbath pictured rest in Him and that what defiles is the heart, not outward ritual, a higher standard than the Pharisees' outward show.
teachings.text:
The chapter ends with two more challenges by the scribes and Pharisees to Jesus and His correction of their error.

First, they accuse Jesus and His disciples of not being pious enough to fast, and use the austere ministry of John the Baptist and his followers fasting to lend more credence to their own self-righteous fasting. To build a stronger "got ya" against Christ. And once again, Christ answers them with unassailable doctrine. How can they fast in the presence of the bridegroom? They celebrate while He is with them, and will fast once He's gone.

Jesus says one doesn't patch an old garment with new cloth, or place new wine in old skins, as a parable to what would happen. The cloth would rend from the inflexibility of the new cloth. The wine, fresh juice would ferment and tear the old skins. So to, He is saying He isn't there to "patch" the old failed ways of the Pharisees, to mend the old law. He's there to fulfill it and make it new again.

Mark shifts to another instance of the so-called holy men challenging Christ and the behavior of His disciples, as they glean corn in a field to eat on a sabbath. Jesus uses the example of David and his men when they were fleeing his enemies, eating the shew bread of the temple, despite that being reserved for the preists. That the sabbath was made for men, not men to the sabbath.

The Sabbath was designed to picture the rest we have in Jesus after salvation. It was meant to give rest to the weary. To teach as a schoolmaster the truth of Christ to the Hebrews. It wasn't meant to be a way of showing super righteousness by how closely you followed the tradition of man that sprung up around it. As a pups exercise to be seen of others.

That the rest we have in Jesus is the same. It's not our actions that sully us, but the context and spirit by which we commit them.

*All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but all things edify not.*

It is similar to the story in **Matthew 15** where the Pharisees again question Jesus and His disciples, when they don't wash their hands in the ritual way before eating.

*Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?*

*But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.*

A common teaching of Christ is emphasis on the spirit and heart by which we sin, the same as the spirit and heart of how we have faith. That it is the thought of wrath that is murder, thought of lust that is adultery. What our intent and what is in our hearts that God judges when we are His.

This is a higher standard than the Pharisees' outward displays of righteousness, while inwards they are ravenous wolves, full of sin.

However it cuts both ways, where in the trappings of what man sees as outward signs of sin may well be just their idea of what righteous looks like. Who put appearance over substance. Who sin in their hearts, polishing the outside of the cup, but defile themselves inwardly by their hearts.

As Jesus said to these hypocrites “*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess."*

 It is perspective we should all keep in mind.

teachings.title: What cometh out of the man defileth him
teachings.summary: Sin comes from within the heart, so the believer must walk in the Spirit, the word and prayer to fill the heart with Christ's righteousness rather than the flesh.
teachings.text:
In **Mark 7**'s version of this event, we get greater clarity on Jesus's preaching to the people of the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and then, further explanation to the Apostles, where He is exasperated at their lack of understanding;

*Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him; Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?*

*And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man. For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders, Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.*

It is what is in our hearts, our old man's mind of the flesh that wars with the new man created of the Spirit within us. When we are born again, we have the benefit of a quickened spirit, and the indwelling of the holy Ghost, but we still struggle with sin because it is in our thoughts and feelings, still taken by the flesh. By what comes out of us, what originates inside us.

And while this is also a rebuke of continuing dietary laws meant to instruct Israel on the law and the ways of Christ, or similar traditions of man today, like the silly "no meat on Fridays" thing, the important lesson is in how our nature is regarding sin.

We will have foolish thoughts our entire life on this Earth. Thoughts of envy and wrath, fear and lusts. Unbidden. And saying things of strife and contentions, *for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.*

The key is to walk with the Spirit, in God's word and in prayer, that the heart be filled with His righteousness and not our own sinful flesh. It doesn't stop us sinning but it makes it less out of our control, giving it over to Christ.

teachings.title: True fasting and prayer, not to be seen of men
teachings.summary: Jesus prepared with real fasting and prayer to God, while those who deny every word of God and pray to men cannot resist temptation and fast to be seen of men.
teachings.text:
It should be mentioned that before beginning His earthly ministry, Jesus sought to purify himself with prayer and fasting. Legitimate fasting, denying Himself not personal taste and treats, preference and privilege, but actually sacrificing physical necessity that He may focus on the things of God. The word. In prayer and supplication.

How can those who deny that we have "every word of God" and that don't read it daily, allowing other men to be an intermediary, how can they resist temptation? If their prayers are to other men, not boldly going before God the Father with supplication?

They can't.

That's why they often seek worldly power. It's why they fast and pray to be seen of men, and not locked away as God commands. Not going into the wilderness but proclaiming their "sacrifice" to the world. It's why they tempt God.

teachings.title: When ye fast, not as the hypocrites
teachings.summary: Jesus came to call sinners, not the self-righteous Pharisees who boasted of fasting and tithes; fasting is not a sign of righteousness but a seeking of God in times of trouble.
teachings.text:
Returning to **Luke 5**, we pick up with Jesus calling a publican named Levi, who we know as Matthew, who we're told, *left all, rose up, and followed* Jesus.

Now publicans, who worked for the occupational governments of the Roman empire collecting duties and taxes, were looked down upon by the the people under their jurisdiction, who naturally resent their fellow countrymen serving the foreign state against them, and were often as corrupt and crooked as they still are today. Further, Matthew was of the tribe of Levi, who were called to be the priesthood under the Old Testament, and so must have been particularly a pariah in these times. But by faith he answers the call and leaves all to follow Christ.

And for him, as it is for us, his salvation is a cause for celebration. He has wealth and status among others in his profession, and calls those he knows together a feast, inviting Jesus and His disciples.

To this, as is often the case throughout the Gospels, the envious and bitter Jews, in this case the Pharisees, see the opportunity to criticize Jesus, asking why he is hanging out with sinners like Levi/Matthew. To which, Jesus replies "*They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.*"

This is the purpose of Christ's ministry and our commission to give the Gospel to the poor. To the heartbroken. To those in bondage to sin. To set them at liberty with the good news of salvation. Just as Jesus stated in His reading of **Isaiah 61** that we just covered; It is the mission statement of the Lord.

Also detect a hint of rebuke, in that Jesus mentions the righteous in this saying somewhat sarcastically to give a ribbing to the self-righteous Pharisees. They, of course respond with another accusation, questioning why Jesus' disciples don't routinely fast as they do. (They lump John the Baptist's followers in there to lend themselves some of his credibility.)

But, Jesus knows their hearts, that they are vipers. Hypocrites. As He tells in a parable later on in **Luke 18** that seems based on exactly this encounter:

*Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.*

*The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.*

Note that the Pharisees took pride in their ritual fasting, as well as their tithing and temple attendance and all the rest. They saw themselves as righteous by their works and better than, holier than, the humble publican, a sinner who may not have done these rituals and rites but who understands his place and the underserved mercy and grace of the Lord.

There are commandments of the Lord that we are given, things He tells us we must do. We must believe the Gospel. We must share it with others, for example. Then there are things we are expected to do, but not commanded as such. We are not told we must fast, but Jesus tells us how to when we do;

**Matthew 6:16-18**
*Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.*

Notice He says "*when* you fast." It is assumed we will fast, at the appropriate time, called by the Spirit, when we have a need to align ourselves to God's will and build our faith. Fasting in the Bible wasn't a sign of righteousness or a way to get God to do our will, but usually done at a sign of trouble or turmoil in the person's life. A death in the family, a tough or perilous time. At the beginning of a trial.

teachings.title: Of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh
teachings.summary: A tree is known by its fruit, and what we say and do reveals whether our hearts treasure God's grace or our grudges and envy.
teachings.text:
*For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes. A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil:*

True servants of God bring forth good fruit. Others brought to salvation.

False prophets, bad fruit. Damned.

What is it your heart treasures? The mercy and grace of God? Or your petty resentments and grudges? What does what you say and what you do speak of you? ...*for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.* What do you treasure in your heart? It is revealed to all by your behavior. By what you say. By our grace and love to others, and our patience having faith in our reward. Or by our petty hypocrisy. Our wrath and fear and envy. Do we produce good fruit, or cultivate evil around us?

teachings.title: Is this the fast that I have chosen
teachings.summary: In Isaiah 58 God condemns self-afflicting fasts done for strife and show, and says the fast He chose is to loose bands of wickedness and do works of mercy, the sabbath being rest that pictures Christ.
teachings.text:
This chapter of Isaiah is incredibly relevant here. The opening verse, one of the most famous lines used by preachers for millennia. The LORD tells the prophet Isaiah, preaching in the Spirit to cry aloud, to tell His people, the house of Jacob of their inequities. To reprove them of their sins.

 God, anticipating the protests of the people who may resist the idea that they are guilty before Him, says yet they seek Me daily and delight in my ways, they do the ordinances of the law, the works. The sacrifices and the offerings and the dietary laws and carnal ordinances. They delight in doing these things.

They may say, Didn't we fast? Lord didn't you notice? We afflicted ourselves, and you didn't see? Didn't we fast on your day, Lord?

And God answers this rhetorical question for us; He doesn't regard their fasting and self affliction, because they are doing it for themselves selfishly, while they are openly oppressing others. It's not a spiritual act of humility, but arrogant and prideful.

God says to them that they fast for strife and debate. To hold it over others. To judge the righteousness of others. To hold the people bound to a yoke of works-based self-righteousness, not the liberty found in faith.

God asks, is this a fast I have chosen? Did He order them to do these acts of penance on the Sabbath? Is it part of the ordinances given in the Old Testament, the covenant in effect at this time? He asks incredulously, "*a day for a man to afflict his soul? is it to bow down his head as a bulrush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? wilt thou call this a fast, and an acceptable day to the Lord?*"

Basically God is saying, is that what the Sabbath was made for? To afflict yourselves with fasting and ashes and sackcloth? To burden the people? Is this what you call an acceptable day to the Lord?

God continues to berate them, again asking rhetorically, "Isnt the fast I chose to loose the bands of wickedness? To undo the heavy burdens? To let the oppressed go free? "*And that ye break every yoke?*"

The Sabbath was to be a day of rest, that pictured the rest found in Christ. A day without labor, that people could understand that God did all the work so that they could share in His rest. A picture of salvation. Not to bind people to doctrines of devils, abstaining and fasting and weeping and wailing in sackcloth, covered in ashes.

God is like I never told you to do any of this. It is sin.

God continues, saying He gave us the Sabbath that we may do things that a workday prohibits getting done. Feeding the poor, going out and finding them that you may give them shelter in your home. To see the naked and give them clothes. To do the works of charity and mercy that we are called to do as His people. Not self flagellation and misery. Not heaping these carnal ordinances and requirements on to the people who are meant to be free to do His will.

He promises if they do those things he actually asks of them, He will bless them and their light will shine, the glory of God our reward. The multitudes of blessings that would come upon them span the next several verses.

But these false acts of piety aren't it, chief.

God tells us, directly, in no uncertain terms, exactly what His stance on all these made up fasts and acts of communal suffering in His name is. It is inequity and sin. Doctrines of devils.

And God promises us directly, the benefits of doing His will in this, and not our own:

 *If thou turn away thy foot from the sabbath, from doing thy pleasure on my holy day; and call the sabbath a delight, the holy of the Lord, honourable; and shalt honour him, not doing thine own ways, nor finding thine own pleasure, nor speaking thine own words: Then shalt thou delight thyself in the Lord; and I will cause thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, and feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it.*

teachings.title: We are the elder son
teachings.summary: The prodigal son parable is addressed to the Pharisees as the resentful elder son, and many long-saved Christians likewise despise new converts and add works to the gospel of grace.
teachings.text:
Here in Luke chapter 15 we see that again, the Pharisees and scribes murmured amongst themselves, judging Jesus for the publicans and sinners that were drawn to hear His preaching. And again, Jesus shows them in parable that He is come to bring the lost sheep home. He has come to bring sinners to repentance towards God, not the righteous. A physician treats the sick.

And Jesus tells how much joy there is in Heaven when one sinner turns towards God that they may be saved. He offered the example of the lost sheep, and another of a lost piece of silver, and the rejoicing of those who had found what was lost, comparing that to God the Father and His angels rejoicing over every saved believer, even the most wicked and wretched.

To drive the point home, Jesus tells what has become one of the most iconic parables in scripture. The Prodigal Son. This story of falling and forgiveness, the love of a father for a son thought lost to the world, and the joy at his being restored home is well known even outside of Christian circles. It is an archetype used in secular stories, referred to throughout the culture, and the phrase "prodigal son" part of our lexicon.

The tearful joy of the Father at having his son returned to him, all that he'd done forgiven in an instant, has been a moving inspiration to millions seeking redemption in Christ. The lesson that no matter how far we fall, we are still welcome home by God, Who celebrates our return with joy has helped heal so many similarly lost, and brought them home through Christ.

It has moved me to tears to read it over the years. First as a sinner, come to God saying "Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before you, And am not worthy." But especially as a father of grown children, being able to relate to that kind of heartache and love. The shift in my life's perspective, changing the meaning and adding depth to my appreciation of Jesus' words.

But that's not who the parable is addressed to here. It's not addressed to the repentant sinner. It's not addressed to God the Father, for certain. It's addressed to those Pharisees and scribes, ostensibly righteous men, who are casting judgment on the sinners who're called by faith to Christ.

They are the elder son. The son, who by nature didn't rebel and stayed, doing the work on the farm for the father, who was there while his brother went after whoredoms and drunkenness. Who stayed true. And who, feeling entitled by his works came to anger at his father, resenting his brother and refusing to celebrate his return.

How many saved Christians today are like the elder son? Many who grew up in Christian homes, given the advantage of hearing the Gospel regularly, attending church where the Bible was preached, seeing the testimony of their own family, their parents, friends and congregants living out their Christian walk before them, and who, seeing new converts coming into the church, babes in Christ saved from a life of indulgence and sin, often scarred and broken, traumatized by the damage done in their lives and seeking to be healed, and came to resent them? To be holier than thou? Hypocrites? Fruit inspectors?

It's happened. It was the case of the Pharisees, many of whom were not saved by faith but being so immersed in the culture of the religion believed they were righteous by their own works and in a place to judge others. The beam in their eye blinding them.

Even those long-saved, but grown prideful, forgetting their previous state and losing sight of the mercy God showed them, the grace given to their underserved salvation. Thinking they are better than.

These are often those who seek to add works to the gospel of grace. Who push Lordship and outward signs of turning from sin before things like longsuffering, charity, instruction. Who have the leaven of the Pharisees in their hearts, which is hypocrisy.

teachings.title: The shewbread and the Lord of the sabbath
teachings.summary: The lamps and shewbread picture God's truth and word, and religion that forgets their meaning becomes rote practice used to condemn, as with the Pharisees.
teachings.text:
**Leviticus 24** begins with the command to have the lamps of the Tabernacle burn continually, dusk to dawn. A statute for ever. That there is light in the place of God.

And God commands that there be bread baked as a memorial, continually, as an offering before the Lord, and eaten by the Levitical priests. This is called the shewbread, concentrated by the Lord.

The light symbolizes the truth of God throughout the Bible, and so it is never dark before Him. The bread is both the life given the people by God's grace and His word.

This shewbread becomes a means of feeding David and his men as they flee Saul, who was in a murderous rage against the future king. Even as it was offered to God and holy, but to the Lord's purpose, it fed His favored in a time of need.

Likewise, as Jesus rebukes the Pharisees when He and His disciples gleaned corn on the Sabbath to eat, Jesus points to how these things are the Lord's, and not just blind tradition and meaningless ritual. That He is the Lord of the sabbath.

Often religion becomes rote practices, that forget the meaning behind them as the Pharisees had. Using these things to condemn. Jesus says had they understood who He was, that He was present for mercy in His death and resurrection to come, that the sacrifices of the temple were a picture of Him who had come not to condemn but to save, that they'd understand why it was acceptable for them to eat of their work, as the Levites were allowed on the sabbath. Because they did the work of God.

teachings.title: Playing church versus mercy
teachings.summary: God is not pleased with outward acts of religion, ritual and showy worship but with a humble heart and mercy to the lost, the poor and the widow.
teachings.text:
Today, many Christians worry more about the outward acts of religion over the spiritual things of God. They play church, and make a long pretense of prayer, and get into "worship services," getting ecstatic over worldly sounding music, or engaging in fasts and other rituals, that satisfy their needs and excite the flesh, but do nothing for honoring God or doing what He has commanded us.

Dead works and vain traditions, but no mercy or judgment for the lost, the poor, the widow, the fatherless.

**Luke 18:12-14**
*I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.*

**Hosea 6:6**
*For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.*

**Matthew 12:7**
*But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.*

God doesn't care about where you sit in church, sitting in the chief seats, or your religious acts that show everyone else how holy you claim to be. But He cares about what's in your heart and how you treat others.

You can be the most separated person in the pews, but if you look down on others, and hold yourself as better than, you're separated unto yourself. Not the gospel of God. Like these men who inquired of the Lord.

teachings.title: The charge of formalism
teachings.summary: As God indicted Israel for keeping outward forms while failing to declare His law and show mercy, Christians covered by Christ's once-for-all sacrifice must not be hypocrites but do the good works they were saved for.
teachings.text:
Now, having been summoned to His judgment, and having stipulated His position, God begins the indictment against His people, giving the matters of His suit, which He Himself will judge.

God, in showing that He has no need for the blood of bulls and goats, fowls or anything else, begins by laying the charge of formalism against His covenant people.

The religious practices are being maintained, the bare minimum of service to keep the covenant. The Lord isn't accusing them of failing this aspect, but in the weighter matters, as Jesus accused the Pharisees.

God established promises and practices to maintain them as His people, but they are failing to declare His statutes, or to proclaim His law.

The entire point of Israel was to be a light to all men. Not to selfishly reap the benefits while doing nothing to teach all nations as an example.

**Deuteronomy 4:5–6**
*Behold, I have taught you statutes and judgments, even as the LORD my God commanded me, that ye should do so in the land whither ye go to possess it. Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations, which shall hear all these statutes, and say, Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.*

They had squandered their blessings by not fulfilling this role.

**Matthew 15:8**
*This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me.*

God is directly accusing the wicked among His people of missing the entire point, a charge Jesus will use to indict the religious leaders of the Jews.

**Matthew 23:27–28**
*Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.*

As an application for Christians today, the indictment is the same leaven of the Pharisees; hypocrisy.

**Hebrews 10:8**
*Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law*.

Just as the Pharisees had the OT sacrifices, we have the once and for all sacrifice of Christ, and total remission of sins.

**Hebrews 10:17–18**
*And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more. Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.*

Just as He says to His people That he isn't seeking to add more sacrifice to those that they are already, God isn't asking us for additional acts of atonement. He remembers our sins no more. There is no more sacrifice to be had.

**Hebrews 10:26–27**
*For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins, But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.*

Just like Israel in **Psalm 50**, we are covered by the blood. We are his people. But are we bound by the formalism and outward appearance of being clean, while failing to maintain the good work that God has saved us for? That gives Him glory?

Or are we looking over our shoulder, expecting a similar charge to be made by God against us as He is making here?

If we're not declaring his righteousness and glory in Thanksgiving, and showing mercy and judgment to others, loving our neighbor, how are we taking his covenant in our mouths? How are we telling the world that we are Christians when we aren't acting like it? Who does it benefit?

**James 2:14–17**
*What doth it profit, my brethren, though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him? If a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, And one of you say unto them, Depart in peace, be ye warmed and filled; notwithstanding ye give them not those things which are needful to the body; what doth it profit? Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.*

teachings.title: Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers
teachings.summary: Being unequally yoked reaches beyond marriage to every alliance with unbelievers and Christ-haters, and believers must come out and be separate rather than seek salvation from worldly allies.
teachings.text:
Paul transitions to instruction that is very relevant in our circles, being unequally yoked with unbelievers.

Many apply this to marriage and being with an unbelieving spouse, but it's far more broad than that. In a similar way 1 Corinthians chastised them for taking other believers to secular judges to settle disputes, this is an admonition and call for separation. He asks "*what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?*" So many Christians, in desperation and fear, join forces and ally themselves with unbelievers, and not only unsaved supposed agnostics and cultural Christians but actual people who despise Jesus or tolerate those who do.

*And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? for ye are the temple of the living God; as God hath said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.*

Come out then, from them. God is your father. He will lead your people. We don't need anything from the worldly, the mockers, the scoffers.

How can one set of unbelieving, Christ-hating, worldly materialists help save us from another group of Christ-hating worldly materialists? They can't. All they can do is lead us to a place that brings offense and blame to our ministry, and make our gift of Grace in vain.

teachings.title: Walk as children of light
teachings.summary: Heirs of God should not walk as the children of disobedience but be filled with the Spirit through psalms, hymns and thanksgiving, rather than filling their minds with worldly entertainment.
teachings.text:
Are you a child of God or a child of disobedience? As heirs, by Christ, we are of God the Father. And so we should walk as such. Carrying ourselves as befitting our station, in meekness because only grace has brought us in, and blameless in mercy and righteousness, a light that shines so that others may become fellow brothers, who are as what we were.

The children of disobedience are fornicators, unclean, covetous, filthy and foolish talkers, jesters joking rather than giving thanks, whoremongers, idolators. They have no share of the inheritance and God's wrath is upon them, so why walk with them? Why act as they act? Why sin as they sin? Why partake in the things unbefitting heirs?

So we should walk in the light, where the sins of the dark are made manifest. Christ is that light. Making the most of our short time here, in these evil days. Not being as fools, but wise with the wisdom God has given us in his mercy. Not drunk, but in the Spirit.

Paul in a few short paragraphs gives God's will for us that He's adopted. It isn't asking much, considering the gift we've been given. But the flesh is weak and wars against our spirit. Still we should strive for this bare minimum.

And how are we filled with the Spirit? It's not gnosticism. It's not a secret. The Bible gives us answers.

*Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord; Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ; Submitting yourselves one to another in the fear of God.*

Not drowning out your thoughts with music that dishonors God. Listening to others talk, often blasphemy, all day as you work, pushing out the spiritual and filling your head with foolishness and earthly cares. Consuming the latest Jewish fables to talk about with coworkers. Sporting contests brought to you by drunkenness, gambling and vice.

We all waste time, not redeeming the day, rather than being in prayer, song and praise. But the more we walk as we should, the more we are in the Spirit and absent distractions of this world, the easier it is to be in the light, and the more useful we are to God. And the more useful we are to God, the more he blesses us with the Spirit  That's really what it's all about.

teachings.title: Abram rescues Lot and refuses Sodom's spoils
teachings.summary: Abram stayed out of the kings' war, rescued his brother and refused the wicked king's treasure, a pattern for believers defending the righteous without entanglement.
teachings.text:
Abram, seeing his brother in Christ, his nephew Lot, who we saw pitch his tent towards Sodom and get punished being spoiled and taken into captivity by the other kings' armies, seeks Lot's rescue. He is not part of the war of the kings, itself. But he is the finisher of it with God's hand defeating his does and freeing Lot and his people and possessions.

Abram refuses spoils from the King of Sodom, not wanting anything from that wicked man. He did what he did because it was right.

This should be a picture of what action of saved believers looks like, staying out of the war, not getting entangled in commitments with the wicked, not seeking treasure, but defending brethren from violence and having faith in God to destroy our enemies when we do defend the righteous.

Abram rejects the treasure, but ensures a tenth of the spoils were given to Melchizedek as an offering to God. Because all things are God's.

teachings.title: Righteous Lot, the backslidden believer
teachings.summary: Lot pictures the saved man taken in by the world, vexed but mired in sin, whose worldly-raised daughters fell into abomination.
teachings.text:
This is the lesson of Sodom. This is the truth about sodomites.

And righteous Lot, saved by faith while in the camp of Abram, who pitched his tent towards Sodom and Gomorrah, on the plains of the Jordan, representing the saved man who is taken in by the world rather than living a life of separation. Worldly. Carnal. Vexed in the spirit by the filthy conversation around him, but mired in it. So much so his daughters are betrothed to men of the city. So much so, he took wine with him when he was practically dragged out by the angels. His wife, unable to leave sin behind looks back despite the warning, at her old life, and is consumed into a pillar of salt.

Compelled to go into the mountains for safety by the angels, a picture of Christ and the protection of Zion, Lot begs to go to another city, Zoar. Afraid of the mountains and what evil may befall him, even as he had just been saved by angels of the Lord. The backslidden believer, unable to build on the faith that's saved him to escape sin. The struggle many have today.

As everyone and everything around us falls into wickedness. Sodomites glorified and rapists and murderers hailed. Every depravity known to man, even the spoiling of children. And yet we cling to the worldly and the profane, despite knowing better. Despite having the Spirit within us. Despite our being vexed constantly by the filthy conversation of the reprobates and unregenerate man around us.

We are told Lot did take his daughters to the mountains, and sought refuge in a cave. Perhaps his conscience spurred by the Spirit made him wary of again entering a worldly city.

His possessions including strong wine, he in despair having lost everything drinks to a stupor. His daughters, raised in Sodom, raised worldly, desensitized to the wickedness that surrounded them, plan an abomination.

Having lost their mother and home and betrothed husbands, and seeing the wrath poured out on the plains and the cities of the plains, they think it is the end of them. And they decide to lay with their own father and become pregnant. This is the influence of the carnal world that they grew up in. Rather than being raised in faith and taught righteousness. And so this evil seems reasonable to them. And they birth the nations of the Moabites and Ammon.

Remember, the law given the Israelites would prohibit Moabites from the assembly of God, **as a punishment for their maltreatment of the children of Israel and for engaging Balaam to curse the children of Israel**, while they journeyed in the wilderness. Just as the Lord says in Genesis 18 that faithful Abraham and his descendants will keep the faith of God, backslidden Lot's won't.

There's so many lessons to take from this for saved believers living in this wicked world.

teachings.title: Make Straight Paths for Your Feet
teachings.summary: Believers must be separate from the world, accept chastening, and avoid bitterness so their good report draws others to God's grace.
teachings.text:
So understanding this, that we need separation from this world, not to despise our promised blessings for a bowl of pottage, that we not satisfy the flesh in our short time here rather than see our hope for eternity. But, as Moses, *Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season.*

Don't be down or angry with God for His chastening, which as it happens may seem grievous, but understand it builds righteousness so that we may better serve the living God, and bring forth fruit as an example to others.

*Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees; And make straight paths for your feet, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.*

As scripture says:

*I have taught thee in the way of wisdom; I have led thee in right paths. I have taught you in the way of wisdom. I have led you in straight paths.*

And again,

*In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil.*

Following God's word, the hope that we believe on, we are given wisdom, our paths made straight. Not only for us but for those without, who are lame, who are perishing. That they may see God's glory reflecting from us like Moses come down from the mountain.

Be peaceable with all men, showing holiness, the separation we are called for, that our faith obtains a good report, as it did the elders before us.

*Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled;*

Don't allow your burdens and sin, or bitterness at correction or anything to give a bad report of the faith, that others may not be defiled and not accept the grace of God.

We are a holy priesthood. We are heirs to a kingdom. We have hope everlasting. Act like it that others may attain the same. It is the least we can do considering what Christ did for us.

For when it is too late for those we turned away by our bitterness and strife, our bad report and our sin, our despising our inheritance, our lack of faith, they are rejected. And there will be no place for repentance.

teachings.title: Their provocations bless you with separation
teachings.summary: Woke provocations mostly ruin worldly things we should not consume anyway, so being shut out of them is God's blessing of separation, bringing us out of Sodom.
teachings.text:
Tangentially related, I see so many lamenting things done to provoke us into reaction that when you consider it, is based on those tempting us having a lack of understanding. Just as the Sadducees who didn't believe in the resurrection couldn't foresee Jesus answer to their foolish question, these antichrists pushing their agenda seek to annoy and anger us with what is in their power, not understanding the liberty we have in Christ and the understanding of God's law that comes from a faithful walk with Him.

The most recent example is the beer can with a transvestite reprobate on the label.

If you aren't consuming alcohol, it shouldn't bother you or surprise, knowing already it is degenerate by its very nature.

Almost all similar examples of provocation happen in the realms they control, which are wicked and worldly.

- they heckin' made sportsball woke!
- heckin' Hollywood is blackwashing and subversive!
- heckin' worldly music I like are all vaxxers and maskers!
- heckin' social media censored me and stole my clout!
- Disneyland loves homos!

Fill in whatever blank here that applies.

They have limited control over how they can afflict you. Obviously, there are more serious ways they can vex us and endanger us and our families. Endangering us with demographic replacement and allowing baser fellows of the lewd sort to run amuck. Direct attacks done by their own wicked minds.

But most of what they control is outlets for sin. Most of what they "ruin" isn't something we should be consuming or engaged in to begin with. By turning you off or excluding you from the things they control, they are essentially blessing you with separation. God is using these things to bring you out of Sodom.

And so when you're blocked from Twitter, rejoice. When you can no longer consume alcohol because their ads are perverse, give glory to God. When you can no longer stand to set wicked things before your eyes, praise Jesus.

By subjecting you to their provocations, rather than anger, be glad that you now have reason to leave behind their sin, and better serve God, as a separate people, a holy nation.

teachings.title: Separation from heathen practices
teachings.summary: God forbade pagan customs such as enchantment, pagan haircuts, cuttings and tattoos for the dead, and believers should not imitate the heathen.
teachings.text:
Next in **Leviticus 19:26,** God begins to address separation from the heathen practices of the idolators that are being driven from Canaan, and the Egyptians God freed them from.
