Again, a prohibition against consuming blood, specifically tied in with enchantment, witchcraft, astrology (observing times), rounding the corners of their heads and beards, a custom of many pagans of the time and a popular look for religious Egyptians, (think whitewalls and goatees). No cuttings of the flesh for the dead, ritual scaring or tattoos. This is a difficult commandment for many today, who do weird haircuts, cutting eyebrows, beards, etc, along with tribal tats and remembering the dead with ink, "RIP Pop!" and the like. Making it fashionable to larp as ancient pagans.

The prohibition against whoring out your daughters is obvious, but also in the sense of the temple prostitute that many cults utilized. God refers to both actual prostitution and chasing after false gods as whoredoms, and normalizing this brings a land to become full of wickedness.

teachings.title: Bloom where the Lord has planted you
teachings.summary: Like Jeremiah, who longed to flee to the wilderness but was sent to preach at the temple gates, Christians are not to retreat to compounds but to be a light where people are, enduring tribulation with hope because Christ has overcome the world.
teachings.text:
*Oh that I had in the wilderness a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my people, and go from them! for they be all adulterers, an assembly of treacherous men.*

**Jeremiah 9** continues his prophesying, the hard preaching of the words of God against the children of Israel that remain in Judea.

And in it, the lamentation to seek to flee from Jerusalem and the wickedness of this generation, and go to the wilderness, to live off grid, and be away from the evil people, uncircumcised in the heart.

But God calls upon Jeremiah to preach in the city, by the gates of the Temple. To tell them of the pending destruction their forsaking Him has brought up on them.

This same impulse is given to Christians today. To flee the world, to get to a redoubt in the wilderness. To be far from the fallen society that, like just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked.

But, like the prophets, and like Christ Himself, we go to Jerusalem. We are called to go to the population centers and preach the acceptable year of the Lord. To seek that which is lost. To be a light in that darkness.

We can't be a light to others if we are hidden in the woods.

And so we are in the world, not of it.

Rather than coveting a RETVRN to a past we never knew, or a rustic compound in the hills, we are supposed to bloom where the good Lord has planted us. To be a blessing to those around us. To *be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear: having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ*.

Not to flee persecution, and the tribulations that come to every believer, living for the Lord. To *glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.*

**James 1:12**
*Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.*

**Romans 8:18**
*For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.*

**James 1:2-4**
*My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.*

We who believe on Christ have already overcome this fallen world. Because He has overcome death and Hell for us. We shouldn't be black pilled. We may wail with lamentations for our people to repent, but standfast in the faith that has saved us.

**John 16:33**
*These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.*

teachings.title: God is a God of separation
teachings.summary: From creation onward God separates and divides to make a holy people, separating believing Israel after the Spirit from unbelieving Israel after the flesh, wheat from chaff, until the harvest is complete.
teachings.text:
Here we go.

God is a God of separation. The Bible has example after example of division, separating one thing from another. Day from night. The creatures after their own kind. Woman from man. Man from the Garden. Cain and Abel. The descendents of Seth, the sons of God that called upon the name of the Lord and the children of men who did not. Noah and his perfect generations from fallen man. The animals of the ark. The nations of Noah's sons. The people of Babel and their languages. The habitations of the nations. Abraham out of Ur. Ishmael and Isaac. Jacob and Esau. Joseph and his brothers. Hebrews out of their land and into Egypt. Out of Egypt and back in the land. The covenant with Moses that they would be a holy people. Separated from other nations.

Even here, in Numbers, each tribe separated and counted. And the Levites separated even further.

**Luke 12:51**
*Suppose ye that I am come to give peace on earth? I tell you, Nay; but rather division:*

The division. The separation. Making holy a people of God. Separating Israel from Judah. And Jesus from the root of Jesse. Believing Israel from the non-believing Jews. The tares from the wheat. Sheep from goats. Israel after the flesh and Israel after the Spirit. Unfruitful branches cut off and cast into the fire. The election in Christ chosen to be graft in.

**Deuteronomy 7:6**
*For thou art an holy people unto the LORD thy God: the LORD thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.*

**Isaiah 62:12**
*And they shall call them, The holy people, The redeemed of the LORD: and thou shalt be called, Sought out, A city not forsaken.*

**1 Peter 2:9**
*But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light;*

Winnowing the chaff from the wheat. The earth is His threshing floor. The harvest is ongoing. We are in the last days, and have been since the first fruit of Christ, and the harvest of 5,000 made by the disciples on Pentecost. We shall bring in the sheaves for the Lord. To Him the increase. Until the fullness of the harvest comes in.

Amen

teachings.title: When family despises your walk with Christ
teachings.summary: As Michal despised David's worship, worldly loved ones may resent a believer's walk with Christ, and Jesus warns that family and the cares of this world must not come before discipleship.
teachings.text:
**Numbers 4:15**
*And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation.*

Poor Uzzah. If only he had been a Levite of the line Kohath.

David builds the tabernacle in his city, and his houses and settles the ark of the Lord in Jerusalem. Leading the congregation with music and singing. Glad to be going to the house of the Lord.

But Saul's daughter, Michal, David's first wife, looks upon him and despises him.

The hatred of Michal towards David is personal, obviously their turbulent history and his taking her father's place act as kindling for it. But the spark seems to be seeing David gladly worshipping the Lord. Joining in the assembly. Getting right and doing things for God.

In a like manner, we may often experience this reaction as saved believers, where a family member or someone close to us resents our relationship with Jesus and our going to church, reading the Bible, cleaning up our life.

Bringing the word of God, the holy Spirit, the love of Christ, into our lives can make worldly people despise us.

Jesus came to bring division.

**Luke 14:26-27**
*If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.*

A man may come to Jesus, and despise not his wife or family, and so, not be a disciple. A believer can be saved and yet be caught up in the cares of this world, being influenced by others who pull him away from living for Christ.

**Matthew 13:22**
*He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.*

If you seek to be more than just be saved, a good husband and father, wife and mother, but instead wish to do great things for the Lord, don't neglect Jesus' warning.

And as Paul wrote, in his opinion; **1 Corinthians 7**:

*It is good for a man not to touch a woman. Nevertheless, to avoid fornication, let every man have his own wife, and let every woman have her own husband. Let the husband render unto the wife due benevolence: and likewise also the wife unto the husband.*

*But I speak this by permission, and not of commandment. For I would that all men were even as I myself. But every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that.I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, it is good for them if they abide even as I.*

Marriage is honorable. Family is a blessing. But be aware that your commitment to Christ can put you at emenity with your loved ones. Division; **Luke 12:53:**

*The father shall be divided against the son, and the son against the father; the mother against the daughter, and the daughter against the mother; the mother in law against her daughter in law, and the daughter in law against her mother in law.*

teachings.title: Building the wall while the mockers scoff
teachings.summary: Like Nehemiah's builders, believers growing in sanctification will be mocked even by family, and must keep building, put on the whole armour of God, and pray for one another.
teachings.text:
And so as the construction continued, and the mockers increased their scorn and ridicule, it became apparent to the scorners, like Sanballat, a governor in Samaria, Tobiah the Ammonite, that the Jews were serious in the endeavor.

The wall wasn't finished but it was getting there.

In our Christian life, we may experience initial scoffing by our friends, family and neighbors. People who doubt our conversion because they know us. The old man. And those things they say may throw us off our course. Make us doubt ourselves.

When Tobiah says a fox could topple their wall, it's like when a brother or parent scoffs at our faith and our attempts to get right. But we see from Nehemiah how to handle this. To turn their reproach upon their own head. To trust in the Lord.

Their mocking comes not only at our expense, but it reveals in themselves to their own sin and iniquity.

**Proverbs 29:27**
*An unjust man is an abomination to the just: and he that is upright in the way is abomination to the wicked.*

Jesus says He came into this world to divide it. Even family.

**John 3:19-21**
*And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.*

So the scoffers in Nehemiah's day set their minds to violence in an effort to stop the construction. This also can be how some people will react to your sanctification, as you build upon the foundation Christ has laid in your heart. So we must stand watch, and continue building. We put on the whole armor of God.

**Ephesians 6:10-18**
*Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil. For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand. Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness; And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked. And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints*

The prayers of the saints are our spears, always at the ready. Pray for one another to stand strong to the mocking. Our brothers and sisters in Christ. Knowing we have each other's back, as the people of Jerusalem did against the mockers.

teachings.title: Be not envious against evil men
teachings.summary: Solomon's later proverbs read like Paul's epistles in teaching believers not to envy or keep company with evil men nor partake of their sins, showing the single unified wisdom of God throughout the Bible.
teachings.text:
Deep in the meat of the word, the heart of these sayings, we really can capture the themes that have been being hammered, again and again, and see the Gospel of hope that is in Proverbs.

To me, these later sections seem almost to be a New Testament epistle, and much of it would fit there.

The Epistles of Paul highlight the implications of salvation on the Christian life. Solomon's wisdom does much the same thing.

**2 Corinthians 6:14**
*Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers: for what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?*

Be not envious of evil men, or desire to be with them. Don't take part in another man's sin.

**1 Timothy 5:22**
*Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins: keep thyself pure.*

**1 Corinthians 5:11**
*But now I have written unto you not to keep company, if any man that is called a brother be a fornicator, or covetous, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, or an extortioner; with such an one no not to eat.*

**Ephesians 5** is full of such wisdom;

*Let no man deceive you with vain words: for because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience.Be not ye therefore partakers with them*...

*And have no fellowship with the unfruitful works of darkness, but rather reprove them.*..

*See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil. Wherefore be ye not unwise, but understanding what the will of the Lord is. And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit*...

*Nevertheless let every one of you in particular so love his wife even as himself; and the wife see that she reverence her husband.*

The wisdom of God is clear and consistent throughout the Bible. We are given parable, story, sayings that all convey a single, unified message. The way of God. His ways are not our ways, yet we may know Him, because He has shown us in His word. What a blessing.

teachings.title: Take up the cross: the call of discipleship
teachings.summary: Beyond salvation, discipleship means being willing to forsake family, possessions and life itself for Christ, a cost Jesus increasingly preached as the cross neared.
teachings.text:
Another message Jesus began mentioning increasingly as His time drew near, was that of discipleship. Of not just salvation by faith, and the fulfilment of the promise made of God for a Christ, but that of those who would pick up their cross and follow Him. Those who would, for love of Him, forsake everything to serve Him, and what that would mean.

He called Peter, Andrew, James and John to be fishers of men, to forsake family and the family's business as fishermen, and they left all. Due to Jesus' intervention, they filled their nets so much so the boats began to capsize. They had the richest catch of their lives, and left it behind on the beaches of Galilee for others, in order to become disciples of Christ.

This wasn't for everyone who believed. And it certainly divided off those who were there only for the spectacle; the signs and wonders, the miracles performed, the fiery sermons preached, the dead brought back to life and demons cast out.

Jesus frequently warns there's a cost for following Him. His hard sayings brought division, and offended many that they no longer followed. His telling them that they'd be persecuted, brought before magistrates and beaten in synagogues for His name's sake, that they would see prison, and possible death for preaching the Gospel.

Jesus told those who were faithful to follow Him and be His disciples that they should go out, among the highways and hedges, with nothing but the clothes on their back and the sandals on their feet, and want for nothing, to live on faith that God would provide. To leave their family, friends, the towns they knew, the sins they were comfortable in, the ways of their former life, that they may seek rewards in Heaven, afar off, ministering to the the poor in spirit, that they may come to know the truth of God. To do more than simply believe and be saved. To do more than be in the Kingdom of Heaven, but to help reign over it. To be willing to live for Christ and not themselves.

This wasn't for everyone. Many in the crowds who believed fell away. Like the seed that falls on rocky soil that grows up with shallow roots and fades away in the heat of the sun.

Some, in the joy of their salvation and the hope they were filled with tarried longer, seeking to do some service for Christ, only to fade by and by, consumed by the cares of this world.

Many are called but few chosen. The harvest is ripe but the laborers few. The spirit willing, but the flesh weak.

It is in this context that we see Jesus, on the road to Jerusalem and the looming weight of the cross already heavy on His shoulder, and He turns to the masses that are behind Him, some saved. Some already having given up much to follow Him. Some who believed unto salvation and others unsure. And gadflies and haters of God, seeking that He fall in some way that they could accuse Him. These same sort of mixed multitudes that had been with Him throughout His ministry.

And it is in this context that He speaks to them, recorded here in Luke chapter 14.

Jesus says essentially, if anyone comes to Him, to be His disciples, and hates not his family, not only his father and mother and wife, but his brothers and sisters and his own children, and more than that, his own life, he cannot be His disciple.

Understanding that Jesus doesn't mean that we should hate them, or ourselves, but that we be willing to give them up and more, our very lives because we love Him all the more. That if the choice was given between them and Him, a disciple would choose Christ.

He says of you're not earnestly expecting to bear your cross, the implement of death used by the Romans, the equivalent to this first century group of people, pre-crucification, pre-resurrection, to saying a firing squad, an electric chair, lethal injection. If you're not willing to be hung from a tree in public, a gazingstock in death for those passersby, a horrific sight they may have seen themselves as it was common, Jesus says, if they would follow Him they must be prepared to face.

teachings.title: Count the cost; salt that loses savour
teachings.summary: Jesus urged the crowds to count the cost before following Him, for a disciple who falls away is mocked and like salt without savour is cast out.
teachings.text:
Jesus turns to this mass of people and says, sit down first and count the cost. Consider the price. For if they begin their discipleship and fall away in due time, they will be mocked. Ridiculed. Their faith doubted. The cause of Christ given a bad report, but more, they themselves would be seen as foolish. Taken by a trend, their service just a fad. That they didn't mean all they said.

Like a king, knowing he faces overwhelming odds, would sue for peace having scouted and reckoned the cost of war, Jesus is begging they likewise consider if they can follow after Him.

Jesus says; *Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour wherewith shall it be seasoned with?* You may be useful to the Lord. You may, with the best of intentions and the fullest of desire seek to be a minister, serving Him. This is good. But what if in time you lost that usefulness? Salt without savour is not only not useful, but it can't be dumped on the land for nothing there would grow, not even the dunghill, because it would ruin a compost pile. It has to be cast out.

teachings.title: Discipleship, not salvation: count the cost
teachings.summary: The hard sayings on discipleship are not about salvation, which is by grace, nor are they automatically true of every believer; forsaking all for Christ is a serious calling every saved person must weigh.
teachings.text:
This passage can be a downer. Jesus gets real, and many people misunderstand what's being said. Many mistakenly think this passage and others like it are about salvation, not discipleship. This error cuts two ways.

Some believe that He is describing a works-based salvation, that the works of discipleship are a way to earn righteousness and sanctification, and by this false belief fail to achieve either.

But even more common mistake, including among saved Christians, is that Jesus is describing the saved, just as they are. That by belief unto redemption that they have picked up that cross. That by nature of their being given eternal life by God's grace they have forsaken the world. That discipleship comes naturally with being born again, and they have nothing left to do but maybe go to church once in awhile and read some scripture-poasts on Telegram here and there. (Or arguing with heretics online). These passages become meaningless self-congratulatory "inspirational quotes." That when they give up some sin or another, they've picked up their cross.

It is deeper than that, and far more serious a matter to be willing to forsake everything for Christ. To be His disciples. And we should count the cost, soberly and with great care.

This isn't an admonition, I am in no position to judge, I am really only coming to count the true cost of this myself, after many many years of being saved. It is a place that some never come to, or try in youthful exuberance only to fail, but later, in maturity successfully achieve. Jesus wasn't trying to discourage us from being His disciples, but dividing the chaff from the wheat, being honest with those of us who remain.

Every born again believer is called to be in service to Christ. It is time to consider the cost.

teachings.title: Ye cannot serve God and Mammon
teachings.summary: There is no prosperity gospel; part of the cost of discipleship is giving of our wealth without fear or greed, laying up treasure in Heaven.
teachings.text:
This is a theme Jesus has been hammering home; the cost of discipleship.

Jesus said we must be willing to hate our family for His sake, and willing to give up our lives. To love others more than ourselves. To not worry for earthly things like food, shelter, raiment. To be willing to forsake all in service to others, that the Gospel be shared.

And, to use what wealth we have in that same service to Christ. *Lay not up ye treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: for where your treasure is, there will your heart be.*

Of all the warnings of the costs of true discipleship, of truly following Christ, this one against Mammon, love of money, not only giving up trying to be rich and gaining stuff, but giving away the stuff you already have, is the hardest for most people to face.

There is no "prosperity gospel." God provides what we need and knows our needs even when we don't. We may even be blessed with wealth but it's not our own. We are supposed to give all, and yet most of us don't even want to give a 10% tithe to our own church.

This can be greed, and it often is. Jealously guarding our treasure here. That it's where our heart is, not Heaven.

But for many, it's fear. Fear of doing without. Fear that God won't take care of us. That if we give away that which is extra in our lives that others benefit and by our works, God be glorified, we will suffer need. This fear grips especially tight in times like this where the debt economy, inflation and taxation and other worldly pressures weigh heavily upon us.

We may not be called to forsake everything we own. But we are called to at least consider it and do it where appropriate, in the measure called for. To be hospitable. Charitable. To do unto others without thought of ourselves and our own comfort.

In two more chapters we will see the rich young man sit down with Jesus and say in all things he is righteous before the law, and Jesus will say ok, sell everything you have and give it all away to follow Me. And the rich young man will walk away. He was being shown the error of his thinking that he was righteous by his works, and most of us won't be called to forsake all. God knows our limitations and infirmities. But we are called to give. To be as wise as this worldly unsaved steward. To not serve Mammon while claiming to serve God.

teachings.title: Willing to die but not to be inconvenienced
teachings.summary: Christians who claim they would die for Christ will not give a little time to Bible reading, church or soul winning, so we must honestly count the cost and strive to do more.
teachings.text:
The emphasis on discipleship that Jesus keeps preaching, the cost and expectations that he has for us to truly be called followers of Christ, not just saved from hell but laying up treasures in Heaven, should have us all feeling convicted. That we're not doing enough.

Most saved Christians will tell you that they would gladly lay down their life for the cause of Christ. That rather than deny Him, we would suffer death in His name. Knowing we have eternal life and knowing that it was a gift, we would gladly lay it down. Out of love and gratitude for the grace that was shown us.

And we may sincerely mean it, although it's easy to say, knowing that it's unlikely to ever come up. It's a cheap hyperbolic brag. Our lives are not our own and having the comfort of the blessed hope of eternal life means that threats of death are threats with Heaven. But even so we know it likely will never be asked of us and so it's easy to say.

But how many saved Christians are willing to lay down 15-20 minutes of our morning to read the Bible? How many saved Christians are willing to go to church once a week, let alone three times a week? To go door knocking and soul winning? To give what extra they have in wealth and in time to the service of others that God may be glorified in us?

How can we expect to seriously be willing to go to our death for professing the name of Christ if we won't be inconvenienced a little bit here and there?

I speak this to my own shame.

And understand there are unsaved people, people working their way to heaven with the false gospel of works, who do more to help those in need than actually saved Christians today.

 I'll tell you truthfully there are reprobates who for wicked reasons give of their time and their money, that benefit the poor and the needy, more than some saved Christians are willing to do.

Count the cost of discipleship. Understand that Christianity isn't just an identity, a scene, a cheap ideological category to cosplay as, the way political and cultural identities are used today. It is not a set of arguments that we have prepackaged for us to spout off against others who have absorbed and regurgitated the ones they've consumed.

Way too many of us who claim to be saved treat it that way. I say this out of love. I say this to chastise myself as much as to motivate you.

When I count the cost, and reckoning my efforts, I find I do the bare minimum for Christ, and sometimes less than that. If you're honest with yourself, you'll find the same.

There are people like this unfaithful servant who do favors for others that they may gain in this life, and in doing so bless other people more than saved Christians who profess the Gospel and have the spirit within them. Strive to do more.

*He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much. If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?*

teachings.title: Jesus isn't Joel Osteen
teachings.summary: Jesus preached no gospel of comfort and wealth, and the more we read the Bible the more we see what is required of us before we grow comfortable in our salvation.
teachings.text:
This is a hard saying. This is difficult to hear. We are so caught up in touting our own righteousness that we missed the point of having it entirely.

Jesus isn't Joel Osteen. He doesn't preach a gospel of comfort and wealth.

If we seek to grow in our Christian life, we need to recognize the cost asked of us for following Him. And that starts with daily Bible reading and prayer.

And the more we read the Bible, the more we understand what is expected of us. With more knowledge comes more expectation. To whom much is given much is required.

The more you know, the more you realize you're half-assing it. Some will count the cost and fall away, castaway. Like the seed that falls on unfertile ground. Few will strive for the faith and contend for the crowns incorruptible. To produce fruit a hundredfold.

We should consider this before feeling comfortable in our salvation. That we are prepared to do all for Christ.

teachings.title: Honour to whom honour is due
teachings.summary: We are to honour unsaved parents, husbands and rulers and live peaceably with all men by faith, without joining in their sin, rather than rebelling out of fear.
teachings.text:
It is also worth mentioning that God can use unsaved people, people who are wrong on doctrine but in position of authority, to do His will.

Jethro as Moses' father-in-law was to be honored. His advice, considered and heeded. We sometimes see brothers and sisters in Christ struggle with that, where their parents are unsaved, sometimes wicked. Occasionally reprobate. And how does one honor them and honor God?

The same question comes up with husbands with wives who won't submit to Christ or to their husbands, godly wives with unsaved husbands who treat them poorly, and other hierarchical conflicts, such as submitting to government when it is wicked.

God's word is clear and consistent. That we are to as much as possible live peaceably with all men. To submit to the higher authority with meekness and faith, always keeping God as the head, that we don't cater to evil ourselves or join in another man's sin.

People hate to hear that. They want to rebel constantly and be in open defiance of the order of things in this world. Only refusing to budge on the clear fundamental teachings of God, but also giving honor to whom honor is due, and paying tribute to whom tribute is due, and trusting God in all.

*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.*

*And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.*

People are afraid to live by faith. Fear is the opposite of faith. It kills faith. It undermines and leads people to sin, rather than trusting in God to deliver us.

Like the Israelites in the wilderness, people forget what God has already done for us, and so we are easily led to sin, fear and wrath.

But if we walk in the Spirit, continuing in prayer and studying the word to be approved by God, faith grows, and with that faith, judgment and discernment which all work together to keep us from being afraid and reactionary.

*And the just shall live by faith.*

teachings.title: Created for His pleasure
teachings.summary: As Christ, equal with God, submitted to the Father and was exalted, we must submit to God's will and to earthly order for His pleasure.
teachings.text:
The glory and Majesty of the Lord God, by Whom all things were made for His pleasure, and before whom we are not worthy. Who in His magnificent power and wisdom, is perfect and holy.

And it is this same God, to whom only the hinder parts could be seen by mortal eyes, Who when He passed Moses could not bear to witness, and the flow of Moses face from being in His presence made the children of Israel turn away in shame. God who is worthy of praise and service. Serving with fear and trembling at His perfect will set before us in His word. So much so, our submission unto earthly hierarchy is done in submission to Him that set all things in the heavens and upon the earth, to please Him.

As Christ, who thought it not blasphemy to declare Himself equal to God, submitted Himself to the will of the Father. So we must submit ourselves to doing what we are created for; giving pleasure to God.

For Jesus is the equal of God, but submitted unto God, and there by was given glory and is exalted above everything:

**Philippians 2:6-11**
Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross. Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth; And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.

**John 6:38-40**
 *For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day. And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.*

teachings.title: Doing the will of God from the heart
teachings.summary: All submission, of husbands, wives, children, servants and citizens, is ultimately submission to Christ, as Christ submitted to the Father.
teachings.text:
**Ephesians 6:6-9**
*Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart;With good will doing service, as to the Lord, and not to men: Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free. And, ye masters, do the same things unto them, forbearing threatening: knowing that your Master also is in heaven; neither is there respect of persons with him.*

Submission to God is to do His will. His will is knowable in His word, and through His Spirit. In all things giving glory to God, knowing He is holy, and true. That we are created to give Him pleasure in all that we do. To honor Him as He is honored in Heaven.

Hallowed be His name.

For who are we? Where we there when He placed the stars in the heavens and made the leviathan? When the lightning was formed and the thunder of His wrath was made?

God, appearing in a whirlwind to Job asks similar questions of righteous Job. He asks these things of the created who is questioning his Creator.

And Job, having been subject to this glory of God and His Majesty, replies;

**Job 42:1-6**
*Then Job answered the Lord, and said, I know that thou canst do every thing, and that no thought can be withholden from thee. Who is he that hideth counsel without knowledge? therefore have I uttered that I understood not; things too wonderful for me, which I knew not. Hear, I beseech thee, and I will speak: I will demand of thee, and declare thou unto me.I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.*

Husbands submit to Christ. Pastors submit to Christ. Wives submitting to husbands are submitting to Christ. Children honoring parents are submitting to Christ. Servants working diligently are submitting to Christ. Masters, or bosses, who rule justly are submitting to Christ, members of a nation submitting to authority do so, as they are serving Christ.

And in all things Christ submitted to God the Father, that He may be given the world as His footstool, and exalted above all of creation.

teachings.title: Learning to serve that we may rule
teachings.summary: As heirs we learn to rule by serving, obeying parents, husbands loving and wives submitting, and obeying even wicked rulers while keeping God's word as final authority.
teachings.text:
And so, knowing we are sons, heirs, princes to a Kingdom, a better country which we seek, seek it diligently. And if under tutors and governors, schoolmasters until the day appointed, then we are to learn to better serve when appointed in that day.

And we learn patience. We learn right judgment. We learn the law and the will of God that we may better serve those entrusted to us in the Kingdom, by serving those we are given in this world.

We serve God. With our whole heart, soul and mind, we are to love Him. And if we love Him, obey His commandments.

As children, we are given to obey our parents. Commanded so, but with promise that we will live long upon the earth if we do. Honoring them, not just with obedience but in caring for them when they are old. Supporting them in their end years. Paying honor.

God doesn't say "if the parent is good." He doesn't say if they are believers, it is then saved or unsaved.

We are told to love our neighbors as ourselves. The whole of the law and commandments is fufiled in this. How? In service. With hospitality. Grace and charity. Putting their profit above our own. We learn to minister that we may rule justly. We are to be holy because He is holy. And how can he trust us with much when we squandered the talents we were given?

How can we rule others, when we are rebellious and wicked?

We become husbands, and expect wives to submit, as they should, but men are to submit to God, and love their wife as Christ loved us, who did so unto death.

When men don't submit themselves to God, when they don't love their wives as if they were their own flesh (which they are, joined together by God), then wives no longer submit.

Wives are to submit to the husband, and when they don't, their children see and learn to rebel. They no longer honor their parents.

When a nation has rebellious and seditious men, unfaithful women, unruly children, then they are punished by God.

And God uses the ministers of government to hand out His punishment, that the nation either repents, or is destroyed.

And while the unregenerate people that make up the majority of the nation may wax worse and worse, we who are a light unto the world, are told to obey the higher powers. To seek to find ways to please even wicked kings, but always keeping the word of God as our final authority. And by doing so we may be punished. We may be persecuted. We may be thrown into a firey furnace. Or a lion's den.

We may be like the son of Israel, Joseph, sold into captivity and then thrown in prison for being faithful when tempted by the Pharoh's wife. But these things are done so that the glory of God may be revealed, and more are drawn to the truth. And to the Lord goes the increase.

As the prophets were slain. As the Apostles were martyred. As Christ Himself died that the glory of God could be revealed.

And so we obey God. We love our wives. Our wives submitting, teach our children. Our children in honoring us learn to fear God. Fearing God and in faith they do great things. And if the evil spirits that rule this world, the principalities that we wrest with, not of flesh and blood, but spiritual, if they seek our lives for it, then rejoice. It will be to the glory of God, and our rewards will be greater than we can convince of.

teachings.title: The spirit of rebellion
teachings.summary: Rebellion against God-ordained hierarchy is Satan's spirit, yet we never obey a command to sin, and like Paul and Silas our obedient behaviour can win our persecutors.
teachings.text:
"But I don't like it. I don't like being told what to do. I am obviously better, morally, intellectually, in every way, than my parents, than my boss, than my rulers."

The same spirit of rebellion that Satan loosed into the world.

God created earthly hierarchies for His purpose. To shape the clay as the potter sees fit. To make vessels fitted for destruction and fitted for honor. Who is the clay to question it?

Now if your father tells you to lie, or steal. Or to dishonor God, worship idols, to kill. If he tells you to disobey a higher authority, we have no obligation to.

Like Daniel, we do have an obligation to show them an alternative way. God's way.

*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

And so, with every authority. There's never an occasion to partake in another man's sin. There is always a way out, even if that way is to sacrifice yourself that another may not sin, or that those who witness understand the right path, and may be converted by your conversation; which is in the Bible, our behavior.

*Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives; While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear*.

Paul and Silas, in Philippi, offended the Jews and were brought before magistrates, given stripes being scourged, and thrown into prison for the Gospel.

*And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.*

And, in their chaste conversation, in their behavior that showed their faith, when an earthquake came and tare down the walls of the prison, they remained, obedient to the charge.

And the Philippian Jailer, scared not only for his life had they escaped, but afraid of the God they held their faith in, brought them out, and said, *Sirs, what must I do to be saved?*

*And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house. And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house. And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.*

They even remained in prison that the magistrates who had ordered them released in private, would have to come to release them publicly, to the magistrates' shame.

And the church of the Philippians was born and grew, and did mighty things for God, because of the obedience of Paul and Silas. To God and to government, even the government that unjustly persecuted them.

teachings.title: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's
teachings.summary: God uses the persecution of believers to convert even rulers, so paying taxes and suffering wrong is a trifle next to eternal treasure.
teachings.text:
And this is a pattern we see, God using the persecution of believers, even of Christ, to give the increase. God uses the weak things of this world to confound the strong. And in doing so, they are often converted.

Nebuchadnezzar believed, and repented of the evil He would do. Kings came around to free all Judah from captivity.

Publicans, centurions, even some Pharisees, all men with power and authority came to believe, and in doing so were given the same spirit we are. To be good ministers, to rightly judge.

Paul, despite his being able to be released when arrested in Jerusalem, rather went to Rome in chains that he may minister the Gospel to the house of Caesar.

This world isn't ours and the things of it are at best wood, hay and stubble, but the treasure we seek is of Heaven and incorruptible. Things of eternal value.

And when we look at the eternal, this mortal life is given perspective. And rendering to Caesar what is Caesar's is a trifling thing. Paying custom and tribute; taxes, is nothing. God provided us what we have and will again. Even from the mouth of a fish.

And if we are defrauded, Jesus says to not only let it go, but offer more. They take your coat, give them your cloak also. If they force you to walk a mile, go two. If they strike you, give them your other cheek that they may see what they are doing for what it is, and make the decision in your defiance to either strike again, or in shame back down. And perhaps by your chaste conversation be converted. By your stripes they may be healed.

teachings.title: What corrupt communication means
teachings.summary: Corrupt communication in Ephesians 4 means speech in wrath, envy, backbiting and false accusation, not merely vulgar words, and legalists who fuss over a stray word while backbiting have it backwards.
teachings.text:
Some take the admonition against corrupt communication to be simply not to use vulgarity, lewdness or potty talk, but while all those things *can be* the type of corrupt communication Paul's writing about, it isn't what he means. In this context, he's regarding the things we say in wrath and anger, envy, strife, backbiting, tale bearing, railing, false accusations, etc.

Not the words used, as if a naughty word has power to corrupt, but the means and meaning of what's being said.

Is it edifying? Does it leave you blameless to share the good news without embarrassment or hypocrisy?

That's the meaning, and while a cuss word can be something that can be corrupting in this context, it isn't always and discernment should be given. Jesus wasn't using corrupt communication when he said "Raca." When scripture says "ass," or "pisseth."  When Song of Solomon gets a little spicy.

Overly legalistic types lose their mind at a stray vulgarity while accepting hypocrisy, backbiting and railing, being holier than thou.

teachings.title: Swear not at all: let your yea be yea
teachings.summary: Believers have no need to make vows, because an honest man keeps his word with a plain yes or no, fulfilling the spirit of the law.
teachings.text:
As for vows and swearing to God before men, Jesus says in **Matthew 5**:
*33 Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths:*

*34 But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne:*

*35 Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King.*

*36 Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black.*

*37 But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.*

We have no obligation to make vows, to give earnest, and to do these things before God. The law being a schoolmaster brings us to the truth that Jesus is conveying; that a just man doesn't need to prove by vow what his word is, because by being honest in all things, and keeping it to yes or no, and meaning it, we uphold the spirit of the law and its intention. Men will believe us or not. And our vows to these things, be it God, or your life or heaven or things of the earth, all are His and we have no real right to put them up for earnest.

teachings.title: Should New Testament Christians take vows
teachings.summary: Christ and James command not to swear, so believers should live consecrated lives daily without vows, keeping an honest testimony as a witness for the gospel.
teachings.text:
But should we as New Testament Christians take vows?

**Matthew 5:33-37**
*Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.*

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation.*

We are already called to live consecrated lives in service of the Lord. Separated unto the Gospel. And as such, are supposed to be dedicated to the purposes of God without vow, but as His.

And in doing so, we see that the more important thing is that our testimony be without question or ill repute. Blameless. Honest in our dealings that when we say to someone the reason for our hope, we are a good witness for the Gospel that they might be saved.

And while times of fasting or dedication to a specific task for God may be something we do for specific favor, or time offered in service for thanksgiving, we should live separated lives daily, with joy and thanksgiving.

**Psalms 61:8**
*So will I sing praise unto thy name for ever, that I may daily perform my vows.*

teachings.title: Don't make a vow you cannot keep
teachings.summary: God will exact the price of any vow made in His name, so it is no sin to refuse to vow, and plain honesty with yea and nay is the better way.
teachings.text:
*When thou shalt vow a vow unto the Lord thy God, thou shalt not slack to pay it: for the Lord thy God will surely require it of thee; and it would be sin in thee. But if thou shalt forbear to vow, it shall be no sin in thee.*

**Matthew 5:34-37**
*but I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God's throne: nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil*

**James 5:12**
*But above all things, my brethren, swear not, neither by heaven, neither by the earth, neither by any other oath: but let your yea be yea; and your nay, nay; lest ye fall into condemnation*.

**Ecclesiastes 5:4-6**
*When thou vowest a vow unto God, defer not to pay it; for he hath no pleasure in fools: pay that which thou hast vowed. Better is it that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay. Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin; neither say thou before the angel, that it was an error: wherefore should God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the work of thine hands?*

**Exodus 20:7**
*Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.*

People who "swear to God," who make promises to God they cannot keep, who make promises to others based on the righteousness of Christ, swearing on a Bible, and all other manner of ways to vow a vow, need to be careful. God is very clear that He will exact the price for your vow. So don't make one you cannot keep.

There is no sin in refusing to vow in His name. And as Christ tells us, being honest in all your dealings is a much better policy. Let your yea be yea and your no, no.

teachings.title: Words are the window to the heart
teachings.summary: The righteous are vexed by the wicked words of the world, and as Jesus taught, what comes out of the mouth reveals and defiles the heart, so believers must watch what they say.
teachings.text:
David's plea for help, like many of the Psalms, comes from the vexation of spirit in dealing with the wicked of this world. That in a world where believers, Christians, are called to be separated and holy as He is holy, the fallen world full of the iniquity of man troubles us. It is the lot, no pun intended, of the believer.

**2 Peter 2:6–9**
*And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly; And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked: (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;) The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished*

This is a feeling we can all relate to, if you walk in the Spirit.

The vexation is not just bearing witness to the unlawful deeds of the wicked, but in *hearing* them as well.

David says they speak vanity to each other, and flatter, and with a double-heart, speak lies. They pridefully boast. It is the wickedness of words that sees David cry out.

**Matthew 12:34–37**
*O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things. But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.*

Jesus shows us that words are the window to the heart of a man. An evil heart brings forth evil words, and it is those words that condemn them.

**Matthew 15:10–11**
*And he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear, and understand: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.*

This understanding, that it wasn't the ritual washings and dietary laws, cleaning the outside of the cup -but the heart, and what proceeds out from it though the mouth, that makes a man unclean, is often neglected by Christians, today. But one of the most repeated commands in scripture is to watch what you say.

Proverbs is full of advice to remain silent, to not speak like the fool or the froward. To speak truth in all things. To refrain from vain, useless speech.

But the wicked refuse to hear God's word and follow His way. Men *Who have said, With our tongue will we prevail; our lips are our own: who is lord over us?*

Of course, by admitting they have power over their own tongue, they condemn themselves.

teachings.title: Romans 14: the weak brother's conscience
teachings.summary: Romans 14 is not about works salvation or licence to sin but about brothers not judging or stumbling those who hold themselves to higher standards in conscience.
teachings.text:
Romans 14 is often confused by the unsaved with works salvation, but it's addressing those with faith, brothers in Christ, weak in the faith they may be, who add as sin things not inherently sinful, to their own judgement in service to God.

It's also twisted by some who take the liberty found in Christ as a license to sin, saying "The Spirit hasn't convicted me on that" as they engage in wickedness clearly commanded against in the Bible.

What Paul is speaking to is holier than thou judgments of those with higher standards than even God's, or the mocking of those who see it as vain and foolish, knowing the liberty we have, obeying commandments but not adding things like not eating meat.

Both serve God and are acting in their conscience, and to get a brother to stumble in his belief is to occasion them to sin, even if the thing itself objectively isn't sinful.

Basically, not being a fruit inspector and minding your own business when someone holds themselves to a higher standard to the glory of God and their service to Him, even if you know it's a little silly.

teachings.title: All things are good for meat
teachings.summary: Jesus and Paul show dietary laws are vain carnal ordinances, yet the greater good is to love the weaker brother and not give him occasion to stumble.
teachings.text:
Dietary laws amended to the sanctification process of the believer often end in the place where "Pharisees were offended" having made those carnal ordinances into works of righteousness themselves.

Jesus declares the vanity of these carnal ordinances and dietary laws. Paul reminds that in Jesus all things are good for meat (meat means food to eat in the Bible, not just flesh of animals). But the greater good is loving your brothers and not tempting them to betray what they see as separation and sanctification. To not offend their conscience to please yours. To not be spiteful to those weaker in the faith. To not give them occasion to stumble in their walk.

teachings.title: Meat offered to idols and the weaker conscience
teachings.summary: Knowing idols are nothing, the believer is at liberty to eat, yet should forgo that liberty if it causes a weaker brother or an unbeliever to stumble, seeking to build others up rather than please himself.
teachings.text:
In chapter 8 of First Corinthians, Paul gets into an often misunderstood doctrine. It's regarding eating food sacrificed to idols in heathen temples and homes, but it can apply to many other things in our Christian life. Things that aren't explicitly sin, in our knowledge and understanding of both our salvation, and the liberty that's in Christ, and of God's law in our conscience, which is bulwarked by the Spirit.

As Paul says, we who are saved should understand that there is only one living God, and that idols are dead, made by man and have no power, being graven images. But the unsaved man or a babe in Christ, still superstitious of the things of this world, may stumble or be snared by seeing our eating of the sacrifice. Knowing it's nothing but meat, and the pagan practice silly and stupid, we could, in good conscience eat the sacrifice and laugh at how silly the pagans are and give all blessing and honor to God. But if that thing done in our knowledge were to cause the weaker man to sin or not come to the faith of the one true God, we shouldn't do it. It is offensive.

This can apply to the circumcision. Maybe to other practices not forbidden by the scriptures, or that is sinful only in intent of the heart, not in the doing for one at liberty.

I would list a few things, but in doing so I risk offending a weaker conscience.

Ultimately, we should be mindful of others and their infirmities, and seek to build up their faith, not please ourselves.

teachings.title: Liberty, but not at the expense of others
teachings.summary: Our liberty in Christ is not a license to sin, so we forgo things that would hinder others from the faith, which is loving our neighbour and not weakness, though it never means accepting wickedness.
teachings.text:
Now Paul having established this, gets to the heart of the matter; eating sacrifices.

As he's already said it is nothing to a Christian, knowing that the gods they are sacrificed to are just dead stone and wood. And knowing that all things are fine for us to eat as blessings from God as long as we acknowledge that. Again all things are lawful to us, but not all things edify others.

And just as we sit in common with our Brothers and sisters in Christ and are told, by Jesus, on those occasions that when we break the bread and drink the wine we are to remember him, Paul says that by being partakers in this, we shouldn't be partakers of the meat sacrificed unto idols. That although we could do it, there are reasons why we shouldn't.

He draws the analogy between the communion of saints, the Lord's supper, symbolic act when we come together and bless the food we consume together in God's name, in remembrance of Jesus, we are like the levitical priests who partook in the sacrifice of the altars in the Old Testament. And where Christ died once for all men, the sole propitiation for our sin, we partake in the food and drink God has provided us in remembrance of him and that sacrifice.

And if we so partake, how does it look to other people whether they not be saved yet, or maybe babes in Christ, and they see us sit down at the table of idolatry to partake in those sacrifices?

And so we do not exercise our Liberty at the expense of others. We do not seek our own comfort and fortune, we should seek others. We should be pleasing to all men in service of the gospel. We should do without rather than offend.

This aspect of Christianity, that we are both free from all sin in the blood of Christ, and the knowledge that most things people think of as sin is a sin of the heart, because what goes into the mouth doesn't defile us, but what comes out. And out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks. It is our intent, it's the adultery we commit in our hearts. And the knowledge of that is the Liberty we have in Christ. But it is not a license to sin. Because if what we do in our Liberty hampers another person's ability to believe or come to faith, or makes them struggle with the loss of their own flesh which turn to sin when exercised by them, then we must do without.

This is what Paul means by pleasing others. This is what loving your neighbor entails. We are to be weak to those who are weak that they might be strong.

And unlike the Jew who is contrary to all men, we are to be agreeable with all men in God. That's not going along with earthly sins and lusts of the flesh, but it's being cognizant of how our actions on matters can be a snare or a stumbling block for others.

There are many who criticize this as being a Christcuck. That it is this a good natured Christian impulse to not offend that has left us defenseless against those who would subvert and destroy us. That this is a slave mentality of sorts.

But that's not what's being said here at all. When we act agreeable to others to win them to the gospel that is not the same as accepting wickedness in our presence or going along with these abominable people when they seek our destruction.

Being mature enough in the word to understand the distinction is one of the goals of consuming the word daily. Rightly dividing the word of God.

teachings.title: Pray for all men and live peaceably
teachings.summary: Believers are to pray for all men and rulers and live peaceably without fear or wrath, through the one Mediator, so their testimony brings others to the truth, with men and women each keeping their God-given roles.
teachings.text:
Paul, having laid out his instruction to Timothy, and his role in establishment of churches of the Ephesians, and giving some basic commands in that regard, and a warning against reprobate false prophets, moves therefore to spell out a broader doctrine that applies to all Christians. It is how to develop the men to have the temperament that will produce those fit for the office and called to that ministry, and how to edify the church, bringing in more believers.

The first point, praying for all men, supplications, or asking of God for favor, thanksgiving for the blessings He bestows, intercessions that the Spirit may work to bring about outcomes that give glory to God.

This is our instruction for the rulers of this world as much as the beggars, that we may live peaceably. Not given to fear or wrath. This causes many to bristle, but as much as possible we are to live peaceably and without offense, with all men, so we may in all godliness and honesty, bring others to the truth.

*For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Saviour; Who will have all men to be saved, and to come unto the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;*

We are to be a testimony to the truth of this. That our prayers and faith be lived out in a way that brings others to this truth. Doubt and wrath show a lack of faith and offends others from the truth. Simple as.

The spiralling people do when it comes to the cares of this world, or their fearful outbursts show a lack of faith in the same God who they are supposed to be magnifying and giving glory to, as witness to others.

Note that Jesus is our sole mediator for intercession with God. Not spirits of men. Not idols or preists. When we pray for others it is asking Jesus to intercede, God in His name to bless, the holy Spirit to give comfort.

Also, the Bible says the will of God our savior that ALL MEN come to believe. It isn't a select few as Calvinism would claim, and it is our calling to help make God's will manifest.

So men should be holy, in prayer, without fear, peaceable, without doubt and wrath. Praying for all men to come to the truth, even for the government that God may grant us peace, allowing more to be saved.

In a similar manner, women have a role as well. Just as men who are unruly and fearful offer a bad testimony so to do women who dress immodestly, who are ostentatious in their appearance. Not only because of the obvious temptations, but as speaking to their character as Godly women. The two admonitions, one for men and one for women, have the same root context. That we show outward signs of the faith that is saved us to better bring others to salvation.

It's often the men who are most fearful and wrathful, who have the loudest voice in pointing out to women not to dress shamefully. In this regard they are hypocrites. Women should do that which is pleasing to God, but so should men, we have an equal role in winning souls to Christ.

Wear those rolls differ, the Bible says women aren't to teach, because, like eve, they are prone to being deceived regarding God's word. This is just the truth of it, and it is a sentiment found throughout the Epistles, and borne out by experience. This is not to excuse Adam and condemn eve, but rather just clarifying rules and natural tendencies to better demonstrate God's will.

Paul goes on to say that it is in bearing children, and raising them up in a Godly way, that women have the greater influence than men leading the church. That they are saved, preserved and protected, by the generations of children that they bring into the world and give witness to God to, that they may be His.

Too many cherry pick these verses and create an artificial men versus women divide. It is about roles and responsibilities, understanding there are differences between men and women. And we have different deficiencies and negative tendencies that can trip us up in our walk with God.

teachings.title: Servants honouring masters for a good witness
teachings.summary: Scripture repeatedly commands obeying earthly authority and being the best of workers so God's name is not blasphemed, while always keeping God as the higher authority and leaving wrath to Him.
teachings.text:
The final chapter in 1st Timothy, and it is building on the theme of being able to give a good testimony for Christ to others by living like you have the gift of eternal life, not stuck in the cares of this world but growing in spirit.

The admonition to obey earthly authority, to please God and make His glory seen of man that you may give a good witness is repeated throughout the New Testament, from Jesus rendering unto Caesar, to Romans 13 and 1 Peter 2, and elsewhere. This is one of the hardest doctrines for most American Christians today, spoiled by the supposed promises of "Liberty" from the Constitution, and missing the liberty we have in Christ.

We bristle with pride at the idea of being good servants at work, living agreeably with all men as much as possible, paying taxes, tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom. Honor to parents and elders. This doctrine is seen as being a "Christ cuck." Seen as weak by those lacking understanding. Missing that while we defer to authority, we have roles of authority in God's hierarchy ourselves, and that we are instructed to always place God and His word as our final authority.

Often those who cry loudest about supposed persecution and calls for riot and seditions, have abandoned their own roles, or are derelict in their own responsibilities. They care more for their comfort than for their testimony. They live in fear rather than faith. They see wrath as theirs, not God's.

They, not being satisfied with what God has given them, and impatient with His longsuffering, are unable to bring others to believe and so, shoot themselves in the foot and worsen their own condition.

We have one means to lead a nation back from wickedness, and that is the Gospel. Soul winning. Revival. And that requires our being good witnesses to the power of the Spirit and faith that God, who is holy and just, and will keep His promise and restore us.

Paul is writing to Timothy who, living in Macedonia, a slave/caste society, will have gotten both masters and slaves saved, and in the same congregation. We are blessed not to be living in a society that openly enslaves people. But the same admonition applies to us as wage-slaves.

Be the best employee at your job. Even if your boss is terrible. Your employer, even if he despises religion and doesn't know Christ should still be forced by your witness to see Christians as good employees. The best, because we work for God not them. Those of us *under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.*

We represent Christ to the world. We are to be a light that draws men near.

And again, this isn't to say if a manager calls on you to do something that is contrary to God's word that you have to submit. We defer to the higher authority and there is none higher than God. But we do it peaceably, and with humility and meekness, trusting in God to save us should it lead to persecution.

We don't obey to avoid being persecuted, but to please God, and with the full expectation that we might face tribulation when we defer to God's will over earthly authority.

Paul uses Jesus' own example before Pilate, which by His meek silence led to Pilate confessing He was blameless, and leading to the Glory of God in the crucifixion.

*But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into this world, and it is certain we can carry nothing out. And having food and raiment let us be therewith content.*

teachings.title: Give no occasion for the enemy to blaspheme
teachings.summary: Sound doctrine makes believers sober and blameless so the word is not blasphemed, and God chastens His children, as with David, for giving His enemies occasion to blaspheme.
teachings.text:
Chapter 2 is a direct continuation of the same thought in chapter 1 (reminder that these divisions we're not in scripture and often seem clunky and forced). The "But" sets in contrast the reprobates being talked about at the end of chapter 1, to provide counterpoint to what Titus should teach and preach instead. Sound doctrines.

That Christian men be sober and grave, clear minded and serious. Temperate, not given to wrath or over emotional, but instead being calm and measured. Sound in faith, trusting God, and in charity and patience, reflecting the love, mercy, longsuffering and grace God gave them, on to others.

That women do likewise, behaving in holiness, not false accusers, drunken, but teachers of good things. Women being the teachers at home of the children, especially young women, so they may know how they ought to behave and that the young men learn to be sober minded as well. And that they all are given to doing good works out of the abundance of their heart, because of the sound doctrine they have been taught.

This is all to serve the glory of God, to make us blameless that we may share His Gospel. That the word of God be not blasphemed.

We are at Liberty in Christ. We aren't going to be judged by our works for justification before God, but we are judged of man. We are to be good witnesses to others, for the unbelieving's sake. That they may be called by the light of truth we magnify. To become the vessels of gold and silver, meet for the master's use. To be more perfect in our faith. To earn glory in the Kingdom which we are joint heirs.

The Bible says everything else is vanity.

But the occasion to blaspheme God by being a bad witness should also motivate us. That the devil is an accuser of the brethren. A ravenous lion seeking whom he may devour. By our sin as believers, we give him cause to blaspheme God.

When Nathan reproaches David in his sin with Uriah the Hittite and Bathsheba, he says that David's sins of murder and adultery are already forgiven, as David was saved by faith. But *because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the Lord to blaspheme,* God punishes David with the death of his newborn son.

We too face reproach and punishment by God for being a bad witness to His power. He scourges His children for giving His enemies reason to blaspheme. For bringing dishonor to His house.

*In all things shewing thyself a pattern of good works: in doctrine shewing uncorruptness, gravity, sincerity, Sound speech, that cannot be condemned; that he that is of the contrary part may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say of you.*

This ties in with the much-abused James 2, and the exhortation of believers to do good works, that their faith be profitable to others, knowing that a man may judge their faith by their works.

And again it's in furtherance of spreading the Gospel.

We obey the commandments out of love and do good works out of love, that we being honor to the house of our Lord, and build His congregation with new believers. Edifying the church. This is our calling. All else is vanity.

teachings.title: Content in our station, humble before God
teachings.summary: Servants are to be honest and diligent, content in their station and humble, since God resists the proud, so they may win even their masters to Christ.
teachings.text:
Paul continues, again as he has in other epistles, instructing that servants, indentured or employed, be honest and diligent. That they may show through their behavior the glory of the grace of God, who is not a respecter of persons.

*God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble.* The lowly and the high status are all judged the same. *When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom. Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.*

This is a difficult saying, but it is found all through scripture. We are to be satisfied with our station, and be joyous in our salvation.

*Surely men of low degree are vanity, and men of high degree are a lie: to be laid in the balance, they are altogether lighter than vanity.*

Knowing this, and knowing it is God's grace that sets us free, we shouldn't resent our station, and instead be thankful for what we have, blameless that we may win even those who we serve to Christ.

teachings.title: Shall we continue in sin
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Grace is no license to sin; baptism pictures our death with Christ so we should walk in newness of life, though holiness is not automatic as Lordshippers imply.
teachings.text:
**Romans 6** builds on the conclusion of the doctrine of the law of grace, and the implications for that liberty which we have in Christ. That we are no longer dead in sin with the judgment against us in unrighteousness, but born again a new man in the imputed righteousness of Jesus Christ.

Having proven this, that we are justified before God by faith, and standfast in His grace, what then?

Shall we sin that grace may abound? If it glorified God to be forgiven our sin, would it be to His glory that we sin all the more? (Again, as some slanderously reported about the apostles, and those who continue this smear today, calling the glory of God "cheap grace" and "a license to sin")

Again, *God forbid. How should we, that are dead to sin, love any longer therein?*

We are free, in Christ, that when we are baptized as believers, it is into death with Christ, just as when we rise up from the water, it is a picture of our rising with Him into eternal life.

Even so, we should walk in newness of life.

If we are picturing the image of Christ in our baptism, death, burial and resurrection, then our old man, our sinful nature after the flesh should be considered nailed to the cross with Him. *That the body of sin might be destroyed.*

Being dead in Christ we are risen with Him, and risen, death has no more dominion over Him, or us through Him. We are dead to sin but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord. Paul is really hammering this point home because it is not automatic that we who are saved turn from our sins. That the new man's presence doesn't preclude the old man's lusts of the flesh from warring in our members. Our eyes and tongue betray us. Our feet are swift to sin.

If we automatically became holy by our salvation, this wouldn't have to be taught us, and it wouldn't be given us as a reminder in nearly every epistle. If we were given to "show fruit" to prove we are saved, as Lordshippers and other hypocrites suggest, it wouldn't be necessary to explain the old man vs the new.

teachings.title: The spirit willing but the flesh weak
teachings.theme: The old man and the new
teachings.summary: Saved Christians are dead to the law in the spirit, but the old man still reigns in the flesh, so we do what we would not until the redemption of the body.
teachings.text:
And so, building on the implications of our faith, the law and grace, Paul comes to the matter of our flesh, in this world before the resurrection, but after our salvation and the quickening of our spirit in Christ.

Christ, in whose death, we die also to the law, freed then to the Spirit, married to Him in grace. Just as the woman described by Paul is free from her marriage vows at the death of her husband, we are free from sin and death with Jesus. And baptism is a like figure representing this. We are born again, in the Spirit.

But not in the flesh. That's the lively hope we have, Jesus being the first fruits of the resurrection with the same promise to us who believe. That we will shed this corruptible body for incorruptible. The dead in Christ and those that are alive and remain at His coming, all will receive glorified bodies that know not sin. Chapter 8 of Romans will delve a bit more into this, but then the question for Christians is; in the meantime, what?

Our new man, inside, spirit quickened by the Holy Ghost, sealed unto the day of redemption, knows not sin. It can't, being dead to the law.

For as Paul explains, with the commands of God to tell us what is righteous and holy, there is no sin.
