And getting into a back and forth volley of proof text scriptures with someone who's unsaved is unprofitable and vain. Rather we should correct them with love from the scripture they're misusing, showing how it doesn't mean what they say it means using the word of God.

Keeping in mind they may be under a strong delusion, spiritual blindness which is a supernatural thing God does to some. It's why they can't see what you show them the contradicts their predetermined ideas.

Rather, like Paul says of the Jews, lamenting:

*For I bear them record that they have a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge.*

*For they being ignorant of God's righteousness, and going about to establish their own righteousness, have not submitted themselves unto the righteousness of God. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.*

Many of these people are well meaning and have a zeal for God, even if it's in ignorance. We should pray that God opens their eyes and brings them understanding from his word, knowing that *faith cometh by hearing, and hearing by the word of God.*
(Note, faith doesn't come from vain traditions of men but by His word, scripture. The Bible)

teachings.title: It is written: resisting the devil by the word
teachings.summary: Jesus overcame Satan's temptations not by His divine nature but by clinging to every word of God, the pattern for how we resist temptation.
teachings.text:
Luke chapter 4 picks up with Jesus after His baptism in the Jordan and by the Holy Spirit, having been proclaimed by the Father "His Son, in whom Im well pleased."

The Gospel says, Jesus was led of the Spirit to the wilderness, and there to fast and be tempted by Satan, 40 days. It is often overlooked that the three instances given here and in the other Gospels are not the only tests of the devil Jesus suffered. He was tempted 40 days.

Jesus hungered. He thirst. He was weary. He was alone. Without shelter. Cold at night. Hot in the sun of the day. In all ways tempted as we are. But without sin.

And Jesus was led of the Spirit to this temptation, He was not given a pass, was not brought to the temple in Jerusalem to preach the Gospel to an adoring throng of people. He was brought to desolate places where the prince of this world would tempt Him.

Satan, the accuser of the brethren, seeking to corrupt the Christ, and derail God's plan of salvation for the world, tested and tried Jesus that he may go before the Father and say, "your Son is not worthy to be a sacrifice. He is not without blemish." But Jesus withstood Satan, and in doing so, gave us the pattern for dealing with temptation in our lives.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

The Bible says Jesus was tempted as we are. Knows our infirmities and understanding, shows mercy on us. We are not given more than we can handle. If we reject Satan, God will provide us a way.

That way is found in what Jesus used to resist Satan. The word of God.

So understanding that Jesus did not have some special means to supernaturally avoid succumbing to sin, it wasn't His divine nature that saved His human flesh from falling, but His doing His Father's will, and clinging to the word.

Jesus was hungry and weak, and the devil said to turn a stone to bread. A temptation of the flesh. To satisfy the immediate need to please ourselves physically.

And Jesus replied *It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.*

Note His use of "it is written." That man loves not by bread. Not by the needs of the flesh. That there is more to this than satisfying our physical desires but that we live by *every word of God*.

He quotes scripture to put of the devil from Him. Every word of God is all we need to live. (The presupposition is that, in order to be true, we have access to every word of God. Thus the preservation of His word). This having double meaning, as the manna in the desert was a picture of Christ, Jesus who is the bread of life come down from Heaven, and He is the Word of God made flesh, through whom eternal life is given to all who believe.

And Jesus, using God's word, rebukes Satan.

Then, tempting Jesus with power, Satan offers Him the thrones of this world, of whom Satan is god. Given power to influence kings and regents. The spirits that bring wickedness to high places. Overseeing the principalities of the rulers of the darkness of this world. By supernatural means, he takes Jesus to the top of a mountain and shows Him all the lands of man in the world. The devil says to Jesus, worship me and I will give you an earthly kingdom, ultimate power.

And Jesus, again citing scripture rejects him; *for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.* And again the power of the knowledge of God's word saves Jesus from temptation.

Finally, frustrated, Satan places Jesus upon the spire of the temple in Jerusalem. Hundreds of feet in the air. And says to jump, because the scriptures say that God the Father would not suffer to see even His foot dash against the rocks. That God would send angels to stop Jesus from even stubbing His toe, so surely they would catch Him.

*And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.*

teachings.title: Turning to scripture to resist the devil
teachings.summary: Just as Jesus resisted Satan with scripture and trusted the Father to provide, we can resist any temptation when we turn to God and stay in His word.
teachings.text:
Again, using scripture, Jesus turns aside Satan and his temptations.

And the devil departs having failed to stand against the word of God. In Matthew we read; *Then the devil leaveth him, and, behold, angels came and ministered unto him.*

By faith of this Jesus endured, that God the Father would provide. That He loved Him and was true. Not slack in His promise. By turning to scripture, Jesus resisted sin, and was rewarded for His trust.

This is the pattern for our lives. The path we follow, led by Christ. When the Spirit leads us into the wilderness. When we are weak, and tired and hungry. When we are in peril, as Jesus upon the steeples of the Temple. When we are at our lowest physically and mentally, Satan will come to tempt us. And when he does, we can know that none of what he offers us to sin, none of the temporary satisfactions of the flesh, are beyond our means to resist as long as we turn to God, stay in His word, and have faith that our needs will be met by Him Who loves us.

teachings.title: Mind not high things
teachings.summary: Believers must be of one mind and humble, not wise in their own conceits like Calvinists and trad Catholics, patiently guiding those less mature.
teachings.text:
*Be of the same mind one toward another. Mind not high things, but condescend to men of low estate. Be not wise in your own conceits.*

This admonition, to be of the same mind, is repeated in the epistles, that the churches which receive them understand that we all share one goal. Serve one Gospel. Look forward with certainty, the same hope.

It is why one of the 7 things God hates is a sower of discord among the brethren. It is why church discipline exists. But a church that is of one mind can do great things for the Lord.

But more so, see that the same caution to be of one mind, not at variance and strife, is coupled with the warning to Mind not high things, to not put ourselves as better than others, but rather condensed to the lowly. To not be wise in our own conceits.

Don't be a special boy.

If you have wisdom, if you have knowledge, it came from God and isn't yours. Be humble. If facing someone who isn't as far in their Christian walk as you, be patient and longsuffering and offer guidance, because that is why God gave you that knowledge. Don't be high-minded. Don't get caught up in theologies and intellectual pursuit, thinking you're better than the unlearned.

Special boys, your Calvinists, reform types, trad Caths, etc, full of vanity and the wisdom of the world, hold themselves up as better than others, full of hypocrisy.

But we shouldn't be. Rather knowing that we serve God and love others, seek their profit, not our own vainglory.

teachings.title: Condescend to men of low estate
teachings.summary: Do not think yourself above the poor and broken, who are often most receptive to the gospel, remembering Christ humbled Himself for us.
teachings.text:
This is also speaking of not being a respecter of persons in a material sense. Understand that the more lowly and sinful and broken a person is, there's a strong likelihood that they will be receptive to the Gospel. Don't think better of yourself because someone is poor, uneducated, simple, not of your class or status. They aren't beneath you. Be their servants, ministering the Gospel in love.

Jesus Christ who is the holy Son of God, was made flesh, subject to the corruption of the world, made sin for our sakes, suffering the humiliation of the cross, pain and death, the fires of Hell, all for our benefit, while we were yet sinners.

Keep that in mind.

teachings.title: Wine in the Bible and the Lord's supper
teachings.summary: Wine in scripture usually means juice, drunkenness is sin, and it was not fermented wine at the Last Supper, so using alcohol as Christ's blood is blasphemous.
teachings.text:
I won't get too far into the "wine means juice" debate. Most places in the Bible it does, and wine simply means freshly squeezed or preserved fruit juice. Some places it means fermented. This first miracle of the wedding of Cana is hard for many to not see it being fermented, but then would Jesus get people drunken, when the Bible *is* clear that's a sin to even look upon it?

**Proverbs 23**
*31 Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.*

*32 At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.*

*33 Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.*

(Grape juice is clear until fermented, turning it red)

In before Redditards say "They didn't know how to preserve juice until Louis Pasteur!!" That's an ignorant lie. They did, with multiple methods, including sulphur, boiling, wax capped bottles, etc.

But it's a distraction. I can say with confidence that at the Last Supper it wasn't booze, and the practice of using fermented wine to claim it's Jesus' blood is doubly blasphemous.

But let's not get bogged down in the weeds.

teachings.title: Saul was consenting unto his death
teachings.summary: By holding the coats Saul consented to Stephen's death, and even passive consent to sin is sin, so believers must boldly stand against evil.
teachings.text:
*Then they cried out with a loud voice, and stopped their ears, and ran upon him with one accord, And cast him out of the city, and stoned him: and the witnesses laid down their clothes at a young man's feet, whose name was Saul.*

*And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was* **consenting unto his death***.*

*And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem; and they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.*

*As for Saul, he made havock of the church, entering into every house, and haling men and women committed them to prison*.

The Bible says that even by his presence and holding the coats of those stoning Stephen to death that Saul/Paul was "consenting unto his death."

**1 Timothy 5:22** *Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men's sins*

Giving even passive consent to sin is a sin. We are to loudly and boldly proclaim the word of God and stand against evil.

teachings.title: Churches soft on fornication
teachings.summary: Fornication, including cohabiting couples who call it love, is sin and self-harm that churches wink at, though the apostles in Acts made a point of warning against it.
teachings.text:
Many so-called Christians today have rationalized away fornication as not a big deal. Not only do they give exception for monogamous relationships outside of marriage, cohabitation etc, where they claim that since they are" in love" it's just as good as marriage, but even to the point where they forgive the whore-mongering and harlotry of their members. Allowing that leaven to leaven the whole lump as it were.

By being soft on fornication, they not only are being contrary to God's law but they're opening their own members up to self-abuse in this regard. God tells us that it's not only a sin but harmful to us and yet, most churches won't even preach against it except to teenagers perhaps.

It was such an important Doctrine, that in Acts of the Apostles where they are debating the things they can tell other churches that they should be wary of regarding the Jews and circumcision, and idolatry and the like, they make it a point to speak out against fornication. The teaching on it is quite clear.

Incels take the W.

teachings.title: The examples of Israel and the way of escape
teachings.theme: Temptation and the way of escape
teachings.summary: Israel was delivered yet fell into idolatry and fornication and was chastened, as an example to us, and the way of escape God provides from every temptation is found by staying in His word.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his teaching to the Church at Corinth, and reminds them all that their forefathers were baptized unto Moses by the passing through the sea, and by the cloud that followed them as they wandered, the Rock that provided water, a symbol of Christ. And despite this, those saved out of Egypt were backslidden and committed wickedness, as all sin common to man tempts us all.

They committed idolatry and idleness, with the golden calf (**Exodus 32**). They were tempted by the daughters of Moab and led to slaughter by their fornication (**Numbers 25)**. They complained of the Mana and were struck down by the fiery serpents (**Numbers 21**). They murmured and complained against Moses' leadership, and the gainsaying of Koreh was met with instant death (**Numbers 16)**.

These Israelites were faithful to leave captivity, made free by that faith, baptized of a sort, led to the promised land by a cloud and a pillar of fire, fed from the corn of Heaven, they did eat angel's food, and were given the water from the Rock, that was like the living waters of Christ. They ate of the communion the meat, and drank the common drink, and yet they fell to fornication and idolatry, and God did punish them for it, just as believers who are backslidden and castaway are punished by God. *For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.* (**Hebrews 12**).

Paul says these examples are lessons given us by God to learn His ways. God will not allow us to be tempted beyond our ability to resist, but it is up to us to resist, by the path God provides us to escape each test and temptation.

That way of escape is found in our knowledge of the word. By how much time we spend in it. It's why Paul uses examples of scripture to reason with the Corinthians, it's why he reminds us of the lessons from God's word.

If you are facing sin, as thorns in your heart, and you want to be rid of it, or if you are engaging your lusts of the flesh or cares for the world, you will find relief and understanding from God, being in His word. It's the truth. The closer you get to Him the more clear your path becomes and the fewer snares and stumbling blocks there be.

teachings.title: Lamps in earthen pitchers: Gideon's 300
teachings.summary: Gideon's men breaking pitchers to reveal lamps pictures Paul's treasure in earthen vessels, where God works through weak believers so that He alone gets the glory.
teachings.text:
This verse about earthen vessels with the light inside reminds me of the story of Gideon's 300, from **Judges 7**, where God tells Gideon to send home most of his troops before a battle, so that when the enemies were delivered unto them they couldn't take the glory for themselves, he tells the remainder to put a light, a lamp, in earthen pots.

*15 And it was so, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream, and the interpretation thereof, that he worshipped, and returned into the host of Israel, and said, Arise; for the Lord hath delivered into your hand the host of Midian.*

*16 And he divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put a trumpet in every man's hand, with empty pitchers, and lamps within the pitchers.*

*17 And he said unto them, Look on me, and do likewise: and, behold, when I come to the outside of the camp, it shall be that, as I do, so shall ye do.*

*18 When I blow with a trumpet, I and all that are with me, then blow ye the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and say, The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.*

*19 So Gideon, and the hundred men that were with him, came unto the outside of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch; and they had but newly set the watch: and they blew the trumpets, and brake the pitchers that were in their hands.*

*20 And the three companies blew the trumpets, and brake the pitchers, and held the lamps in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands to blow withal: and they cried, The sword of the Lord, and of Gideon.*

*21 And they stood every man in his place round about the camp; and all the host ran, and cried, and fled.*

The faint of heart and fearful are sent home, thousands are sent to their tents. Those 300 who remain placing lamps in earthen vessels, that are then broken to reveal the light and lead God to triumph over the enemy. This is such an amazing parallel to our lives, and an illustration of Paul's point.

teachings.title: Pure religion: the fatherless and widows
teachings.summary: A godly nation cares for the poor, widows and fatherless through individual Christians and their local churches, and both libertarian bootstraps contempt and leftist state dependency are unbiblical.
teachings.text:
You can see how the inherently selfish ideology of libertarianism and post-welfare state conservativism are as antithetical to God's word as the idea of rewarding the sluggard and fools.

The "bootstraps" reactionary spiral comes from resentment of those gaining from their being lazy, being burdens. Neither the cause nor the reaction are righteous.

A Godly nation takes care of the poor and widows indeed, providing sound judgement and aid to the fatherless, through the actions of individual Christians, organized locally by their church.

When that lacks, then inequities abound, and when inequities abound, the beast system will use the opportunity to provide as a means of control and punishment. This creates that left-right dialectical trap so many of us get caught up in.

Breaking it requires being faithful to God and offering help, even if it is providing opportunity for labor for those in need, and graceful charity for those who can't. Not bitching about taxes and blanket condemnation of those trapped in the cycle of dependency on the system.

Especially of the fatherless who know no better.

The grossest thing I have seen, that brought me to hate the Boomer, is their disdain for the Millennials who, having had Boomers for a role model, lack ability, knowledge and judgement.

They laugh at the lack of a work ethic that was never taught them. Lack of discipline they never were shown. They mock that the fatherless they created need YouTube tutorials on tying a tie or doing simple repairs. That so many, being left so ignorant, jumped headfirst in to the false promises of public education and college paid for upfront by Obamaloans.

It is as gross and unbiblical as the heckin' leftism the libtards use to fill those holes, and recruit the young.

**James 1:27**

*Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.*

They've turned this into mocking the fatherless and despising the widows, and hypocritically "fruit-inspecting" others who fail in keeping themselves unspotted from the world, just as we all do.

teachings.title: The whole law is love
teachings.summary: The whole law is loving our neighbour, even our enemy, as Christ did, which none of us can do perfectly, but staying in the word and prayer brings forth the fruit of the Spirit in our walk.
teachings.text:
And what is the whole of the law? Paul again, echoing Christ who quoted Leviticus; Loving our neighbors as ourselves. In all things. And as Jesus taught in the parable of the Good Samaritan, your neighbors are those you meet along the way, even your enemies. And what does loving them look like? Sacrifice of time, material wealth, comfort, status, gain, health, even life to aid them in their need.

Can any of us love this much?

Jesus Christ, sinless and blameless sacrificed Himself, yet while we were sinners so that we may be forgiven. No greater love than this. A standard we strive for, to which we crucify ourselves daily to achieve. Our spirit willing, but the flesh is weak.

So how do we shore up the spirit to bring us closer to following Christ? By being in the word. In prayer. In thanksgiving to God for the gift of salvation. And it is reflected  and made manifest in our walk, through love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.

teachings.title: Obey masters and powers as unto God
teachings.summary: Children, servants, wives and subjects should honour authority even when it is harsh, unless commanded to sin, working diligently and blamelessly because they serve God.
teachings.text:
The final chapter of Ephesians, Paul continues to build on the idea that we are not to despise government, the hierarchies put in place by God, but to honor and respect them, even when they are cruel to us. For we aren't theirs, but God's and what we do in our labors is His.

Be it a husband, a mother, a child, a master or a servant, a king or a subject. If they aren't demanding we sin, truly sin in the despising of God, worship of idols or the blasphemy of the Spirit, and the like, we should in all good conscience work that which we can do, upright. This bothers many.

"How can I obey and serve a cruel and ungodly master? A wicked husband? Dishonorable parents? A beast-system state?" The Bible tells us with faith, meekness, serving God and by our actions, convert the lost.

I find that those that bristle the most at this were raised without proper fear and respect for their parents, due to whatever reason, although mostly having the rod spared or worse, used in anger, bringing their children to wrath. And as the relationship with the father goes, so to becomes their relationship with all superiors, and in the end, their relationship with God.

We should, as Christians, seek to be blameless. Be the hardest worker at your job. Be the most honest. Take the least advantage and support and uplift others, not being a respecter of persons. Diligent and happy. Having faith in God who rewards us, Paul says, *Knowing that whatsoever good thing any man doeth, the same shall he receive of the Lord, whether he be bond or free.*

This is not weakness, but strength. For the powers that be have authority from God, be they wicked or just, those who bear the sword do it to the fear of the unrighteous.

**1 Peter 3**, which echos this sentiment, shows us how regardless the situation, we win:

*13 And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?*

*14 But and if ye suffer for righteousness' sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;*

Or **2 Peter 2**:

*4 For if God spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment;*

*5 And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly;*

*6 And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;*

*7 And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:*

*8 (For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)*

*9 The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:*

*10 But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.*

teachings.title: The whole armour of God
teachings.summary: Honouring parents and working faithfully is possible because we are equipped with the whole armour of God, so walking in truth, righteousness, the gospel, faith, salvation and the word we need not fear the wicked.
teachings.text:
And so we honor our parents, the first commandment with a promise from God, that in doing so we are blessed. We work diligently and with all humility and fear, because we work for God. And we are to remain humble and honest in our dealings, if we are bond or free.

We can do this if we remember we are outfitted with the whole armor of God.

*For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.*

Girding our loins with truth, the breastplate of righteousness, your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, *wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked,* the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit *which is the word of God.*

We are equipped with these things, when we walk in them. And if we walk in them, we should have no fear of the wicked.

We are prepared with truth, not dissimulation, protected from blame by being righteous, prepared to give good answer for our hope everywhere we go, with the good news of God's peace with man in Christ Jesus. Our faith a shield against all attacks, no matter how fiery. Protected with the sure knowledge and confidence of our salvation. And armed with the sword of the Spirit, the word of God, which is quick and powerful, *sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.*

For, *If God be for us, who can be against us?*

teachings.title: An excellent spirit like Daniel
teachings.summary: The Sermon on the Mount calls us to excellence beyond the minimum, and like Daniel we should be so blameless that enemies can only accuse our faith, trusting God to deliver us.
teachings.text:
One of the messages of the sermon on the mount, in fact it's primary theme, is achieving excellence. Going above and beyond the bare minimum, striving for perfection, which means being complete. Whole.

That if we think it's enough to not commit adultery, it isn't, for even the thought of adultery is sin. Even hate in your heart is murder. If someone compels you to walk a mile with them, go two. If they take you coat, give them your cloak. Loving your enemies, not just the brethren. Going the extra mile, excelling, being perfect.

We see in Daniel that he had the spirit of excellence within him. He was blameless in his work. He did more, meekly and humbly, in God's name, serving Him. And it paid dividends with blessings from God and promotion over others. This of course led to their resentment, but they couldn't find anything to accuse Daniel of, except for his faith. And they had to trick the king into signing a law to persecute Daniel for that faith.

This is what we should all strive for. Make them come at us for our faith having nothing else with which to attack you. Being blameless and excellent. Working diligently on everything you do. Going that extra mile. Heaping coals on your enemies by praying for them and meekly and honestly dealing with all. Giving tribute to whom tribute is due. Rendering custom.

Make those that hate and resent you for your faith persecute you for it. Make it the only thing they can lay charge to you with.

And when you are thrown in the lions den, or put in the firey furnace, put you in bonds like Paul, or whatever else they use to attack your faith, believe that God will deliver you.

teachings.title: Render unto God the things that are God's
teachings.summary: Jesus turned the tribute question to show the Pharisees did not give God His due, and the worldly fixate on the Caesar half while the spiritual see the call to render unto God.
teachings.text:
Now, offended by His preaching, the Pharisees attempt to trap Jesus in sedition against Rome. They send their disciples and the Hellenistic Jews, the Herodians, who with flattery ask Jesus to judge whether it is right under the law to give tribute to Caesar. For Jews to pay taxes to the empire that occupied them.

Jesus annoyed at their deception, knowing the wickedness they sought to do, says;

*Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites?*

*Shew me the tribute money. And they brought unto him a penny. And he saith unto them, Whose is this image and superscription?*
*They say unto him, Caesar's.*

*Then saith he unto them, Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and unto God the things that are God's.*

Often the focus here is mistakenly on Jesus saying to render unto Caesar what is Caesar's, which is true. We should, as much as possible, live peaceably with all men, giving tribute to whom tribute is due, custom to whom custom is due. Materialistic things are the provence of the world.

But Jesus is turning the question around on those tempting Him, that their focus should be on the spiritual. That they do not pay tribute to God as they should. They do not render unto God that which is His due.

This exchange can serve almost as a Rorschach test, where the more worldly a person, the more they focus on what Christ says about the things of Caeser, debating taxes and obedience to earthly law, tributes and custom, be they worldly liberals talking about social contracts and socialism, or worldly "sovereign citizens," and their false gospel of libertarianism and sedition.

Those who are more spiritual, looking to the Kingdom, see the focus on giving God His due, which the Pharisees and their disciples were slacking, as so many calling themselves Christian today are, too.

teachings.title: Endure hardness as a good soldier of Christ
teachings.theme: Enduring hardness as a good soldier
teachings.summary: Timothy is charged to endure as a soldier, athlete and husbandman for the elect's sake, who become elect by believing rather than by Calvinist choosing, and to rightly divide the word against cankerous false teachers.
teachings.text:
Paul continues his impassioned appeal to his young charge Timothy, written near the end of his life, from chains. Under house arrest in Rome. Unsure of his future but confident in his fate, Paul seeks to put his son in Christ firmly on the rock of the gospel, and in chapter 1 had recounted that many in Macedonia that he'd won to Christ had turned their backs on him in his tribulation, and turned from the truth of the gospel.

Paul charges Timothy to be stedfast in the faith that won him, unashamed of Christ and the promise of God. Holding fast to the scriptures.

He begs Timothy to be strong in the faith that Paul had won him by, with many witnesses, that is others who believed and were born again, those saved by the word, so as to be able to teach it to others.

To endure hardness like a solider, as he's been called by God to be. Not entangled with any other cause or cares, but the one he's been drafted to.

To strive for mastery, like an athlete. Earning crowns for his victories, without cheating, but with excellence.

A husbandman, enjoying the fruits of his labor, souls won to Christ.

He then impresses upon Timothy these doctrines that he feels are most important, beginning with the truth; *Jesus Christ of the seed of David was raised from the dead.* For preaching this is what brought Paul to be in bonds. Scourged and stoned. Now facing the end of his race, he says he's endured all these things for the elects' sake. For the souls won by the same Gospel he's been persecuted for. That it was worth it all for their sake, that they may obtain salvation in Jesus Christ.

(Note that he is saying they believed the preaching to be elect, and that he endured that they may have believed. Not that they were going to no matter what. Not that they were picked to believe, but having believed, become elected to the promise. This is not calvinism, but how the truth of the good news and the light of the Holy Spirit works in men to bring them to repentance and towards faith in God. That we must endure tribulation to share, that all men might be saved.)

Paul continues. This is a faithful saying, that he charges Timothy to teach others;

*For if we be dead with him, we shall also live with him: If we suffer, we shall also reign with him: if we deny him, he also will deny us: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.*

He writes that the vain babblings and striving, arguments about the law and doctrines not of scripture serve no other purpose but to subvert those who hear them. To keep people from the faith and salvation. It continues the theme of his previous letter to Timothy, about instructing church leaders at Ephesus to be first and foremost good witnesses to the word that men might be saved. Here too, he is seeking to reinforce this idea, especially where there are those like Hymenaeus and Philetus, teaching false doctrines and damnable heresies such as the resurrection having already been past. (Hymenaeus is the same heretic who Paul said he had given over to Satan for his blasphemy in 1 Timothy 1:20)

Like Phygellus and Hermogenes, who ashamed of Paul's bonds, abandoned him and the calling, weakening the power of the Gospel for those who witnessed their shame and fear.

These false teachers and weak leaders, subverting and deserting, are like cankers. Their striving and arguments like sores that fester and eat away at the word, leading men to damnation.

Instead he charges Timothy to study to be approved by God rightly dividing the word that he may be able to stablish the faith of many, where these heretics overthrow the faith of some.

*Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth sure, having this seal, The Lord knoweth them that are his. And, let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity.*

Again, God knows who are His, but he lets, allows, every one that calls upon the name of Christ be saved.

teachings.title: How to become a vessel meet for the master
teachings.theme: Vessels meet for the master's use
teachings.summary: We sanctify ourselves by fleeing youthful lusts, following righteousness, avoiding foolish questions, and gently teaching those in error so they may come to the truth.
teachings.text:
And how does one sanctify themselves? How can we as believers be more than a wooden or clay pot, but become tools for God's glory?

*Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart.*

*But foolish and unlearned questions avoid, knowing that they do gender strifes.*

*And the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men, apt to teach, patient, In meekness instructing those that oppose themselves; if God peradventure will give them repentance to the acknowledging of the truth;*
*And that they may recover themselves out of the snare of the devil, who are taken captive by him at his will*.

We study His word. We know the answers to good questions that we may give meek and ready reason for the hope we have. Being patient. Charitable, loving people with the same grace shown us by God. Not striving, or argumentive, but gentle that those who are in sin come to the truth, and be saved.

This is the meat of the word. It is next level stuff, not easily obtained, but that we must seek to be further transformed for the master's use. Praying for the wisdom and faith to grow in discipleship. Letting go of the cares of this world, that we may live in honor and glory in the next.

teachings.title: The sower: deep roots in good ground
teachings.summary: Jesus used natural things to teach the spiritual, which the natural man cannot discern, and saved believers can be stony or thorny ground unless they grow deep roots in God's word.
teachings.text:
In Mark 4 we see another parallel passage, this time with [Matthew 13](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/5194) which we studied a few weeks ago. (it's repeated in **Luke 8** as well, which God willing we shall see soon)

The parable of the sower is another instance of the nature of creation existing that Jesus, the word of God though whom all things were created, may use it as example to explain the heavenly things of God. The physical to understand the spiritual.

For we who are saved, the greater lesson is how we rightly divide the word, understanding that His words are spirit. That His words are eternal life, and what that means. That creation speaks the word of God for those with ears to hear and eyes to see. Who aren't without deep roots, who aren't choked out by thorns. That we may be fertile soil and bring forth fruit after our kind, 100 fold.

*And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them*.

Jesus used clearly discerned pictures of the natural, the physical, to help us understand the spiritual, the unseen, that we who are seeking God's truth or who have received the quickening of our spirit may receive faith, which the Bible says *is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.*

He uses the seen to give us insight to the unseen. This is what I was getting at [yesterday](https://t.me/HouseOfWews2/6127).

But to the carnally minded all things are physical, literal. Materialists see Jesus parables as Nicodemus did; taken to absurd levels or autistic literalism and missing the actual spiritual application.

This is what the Bible means by "*the natural man receiveth not the things of the Spirit of God: for they are foolishness unto him: neither can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned."*

The natural man is earthly. They rely on the wisdom of man. They lean unto their own understanding. They are those by the wayside where the word is sown and *Satan cometh immediately, and taketh* it away.

And as we see in the parable of the sower, as Jesus explains, there are saved Christians who are the stoney ground. They hear the word and believe, but having nothing to take hold of, being unprofitable, without a church, without reading their Bible, without seeking to learn the deeper things of God, *and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word's sake, immediately they are offended.*

There are Christians who hear the word and are saved, but are among thorns, the cares of the world. They allow covetousness and lust to choke them out, and become unable to bear fruit. To get more people saved by their example. Unprofitable to God or to others.

We should seek to grow roots, deep in fertile soil which is God's word and His ways that we may win souls to Christ and bring in the harvest for the Lord.

teachings.title: Esau sold his birthright for pottage
teachings.summary: Carnal Christians who trade their blessings for fleshly pleasures are like Esau, keeping sonship but losing blessings here and in the kingdom.
teachings.text:
Issac, at 60 years old, finally becomes a father. In an echo of his own birth, Rebekah is as barren as Sarah was. Yet God intervenes, and the couple conceive twin boys.

As God says to Rebekah, there are two nations striving within her. One shall be strong, and the elder will serve the younger.

Esau, the first born, hair red as the pottage he'd sell his birthright for. Red is the meaning of Edom. Jacob, second born, holding on to Esau's foot, as they are taken from their mother.

*And the boys grew: and Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.*
*And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: but Rebekah loved Jacob.*

God wastes no time on irrelevant details. Isaac's life story is briefly skimmed over. Only the details of the inheritance and blessing matter to the story God is telling. Of the elder serving the younger. Of the law and of faith.

And so, we come to adult Esau and Jacob, men established as a hunter, and a man of the field, while the younger tends flocks, living in tents. No great hero and hunter, proficient with weapons like his elder brother, but a plain man.

Jacob makes a red pottage, a lentil soup. Esau, hungry and tired, saying "*Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage; for I am faint*."

Most interpret this to just mean normal hunger. Not truly fainting or starving in a serious sense. Just ravenous from being out in the field hunting, and wanting to please his flesh by eating the pottage.

Jacob says he will feed his brother in exchange for his birthright. And despising his birthright, that is not caring about it, willing to trade it for a momentary satisfaction of the flesh, Esau agrees.

Paul uses this illustration in **Hebrews 12** regarding fornicators among the believers, who have the inheritance but lose the blessings that come with the birthright we share in Christ Jesus for the same momentary satisfaction of the flesh. That later, though he repented of giving away his inheritance by law to his younger brother, having a change of heart too late, and losing the eventual blessings meant for him.

Christians who live carnally, after the flesh, despising their birthright received through Christ, losing blessings of God for their own morsel of meat, a simple bowl of pottage, are like Esau. And while we still retain sonship, and gain a share in the kingdom, the blessings we lose here in this life and in the time to come are lost or diminished, regardless of how tearfully we may regret it when our flesh dies. It's a grave warning.

We know, having hindsight what a fool Esau, now Edom was. Yet how many times do we do the same, for much less than even a bowl of lentils?

teachings.title: The World Hates an Evil Report of Sin
teachings.summary: As Joseph's brothers hated him for his evil report, the world hates faithful Christians because preaching against sin exposes their deeds.
teachings.text:
**Genesis 37** begins the tale of Joseph and Judah, the other brothers and how the sons of Jacob came to be in Egypt. The generations of Israel, told by God through Moses. In this narrative, there lays prophecy of Christ Jesus, both as a figure in Joseph and in the blessing upon Judah, which we will see later near the end.

But keeping in mind the picture of Jesus in Joseph and the traits of man in the brothers, especially Judah/Jews of Christ's time, there's a lot to digest.

First, we are given the timing and situation; Joseph, the first son born unto Rachel, Jacob's first love, and so the father's favorite. Joseph, out with his half brothers tending the flocks returns to his father, bringing an "evil report." Bringing word to the father that the children are in sin.

And the brothers hate him for it.

Much the same way today the world hates a faithful Christian for the reminder of their sin we bring. The light shined on their inequity. As Jesus says in **John 3:20**:

*For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.*

Christians standing fast against sin bring an evil report of the wicked hearts of men. The world resents it.

**John 15:18** I*f the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.*

Joseph's brothers hated him for the same reason. Sinners hate preaching against sin. Standards and morality. God's word, which convicts them. Christians who bring an evil report to their deeds.

And like Joseph's brothers, the world plots and schemes ways to shut us up. To sully Christ's name by our own failings. To discredit God's word. To subvert His people. To call good evil and evil good.

[Isaiah 5:20](https://t.me/ApeMtn37/3516)
*Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!*

teachings.title: Work Faithfully Like Joseph Even in Prison
teachings.summary: Saved workers should be like Joseph, working hard and doing right in every condition, trusting God to bless their hand.
teachings.text:
Now catching up with Joseph, we see the contrast between him and his brother Judah. Who being free and rich, fell in to the wrong crowd, was taken by lust and had sons slain by the Lord for their wickedness, while Joseph was a slave who strived to do right in the eyes of the Lord and was blessed exceedingly.

As a worker, we who are saved should strive to be as Joseph. Working hard, loyally and having faith God will bless our hand if we do. Joseph in the worst of conditions, even prison, rises to the top because of his faith.

The wife who trapped him with a lie did a wicked evil to him. He could have given in, he could have cursed God for his fate, he could have been bitter or angry. Instead he just does what's right even in jail. And God continues to bless him.

**Philippians 4:12**

*I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.*

teachings.title: God's Will Is Found in His Word
teachings.theme: The will of God in His word
teachings.summary: Those seeking God's will or more faith should start with His word, which gives faith and plainly states His will for His children.
teachings.text:
People often say they are waiting on the revelation of the "will of God" to make decisions or a sign to show them the way. They don't know if they have the faith to make a change in their lives or the understanding to do what God wants in a given situation. They express fear at circumstances or tribulation that befalls them. They may pray for guidance and strength, but struggle to find what God wants for their life.

The Bible tells us where faith comes from. It tells us God's will for us as His children. It gives instruction for how to gain knowledge, insight, understanding and peace. How to live, what our roles are. To obey those in charge of us, to love those under us. In all things, doing it for God, for that is His will. To abstain from fornication. To flee Idolatry. To trust in Him to guide us. To live by faith and to gain faith by His word. (The just shall live by faith)

If you are feeling rudderless. If you are searching for more faith. If you don't know what you should do. Start with the word. Make sure you are doing the things God has told us are His will (obviously starting with obeying the Gospel, and believing on the Lord Jesus Christ).

Tomorrow's study on Hebrews 11, the Hall of Faith heroes of the OT, will demonstrate how faith led them to serve the will of God.

teachings.title: Faith Without Works Is Dead
teachings.summary: Justified before God by Christ's blood, believers show their faith before men by works, while those who make works their justification damn themselves.
teachings.text:
Now, the expression of faith is found by obeying the will of God. By this a man's faith is justified before men. Just as the OT saints listed in **Hebrews 11** believed and their faith was counted for righteousness, and by faith their works showed to others the power of God's promises.

So too, we are to live our faith. For faith without works is dead, being alone. We may be justified by the blood of Christ before God, but if we hide that faith under a bushel, or we bury that which we've been trusted rather than gain an increase for the Lord, our faith is fruitless. Dead.

The exhortation of James 2 to live out our faith and in doing so, help those in need, sharing that faith that they may come to the same and live, is a beautiful reminder of our calling.

Those that twist it to make works their means of justification before God, damn themselves and put Christ to an open shame, for their dead works are without faith. Disobedient to the Gospel. Perishing.

teachings.title: The fathers have eaten sour grapes
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 18 teaches that God judges each man on earth by his own sins, so we cannot blame our troubles on our fathers but must walk righteously ourselves.
teachings.text:
It's important in understanding this particular prophecy of God that this is not about salvation, it is about life on this earth, and soul in this sense means the person. Spirit and body together form a soul.

Now with that understanding, let us consider the opening verse. *What mean ye, that ye use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying, The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge?*

The saying refers to the idea that the children of Israel are claiming that God is judging unfairly by punishing them for what their parents did. What their immediate forefathers got up to. That they ate sour grapes but it's the children whose teeth are on edge.

It's important to keep this chapter of Ezekiel in mind when we're looking at the boomer question. God judges us fairly on this earth, saved or unsaved. We may suffer from the sins of a father, but our own inequities are what we are punished with.

Just as a just man may have an unjust son, so too can an unjust man have a just son. It is the keeping of the statutes and doctrines of God that prolongs ones life and brings blessings to it. It is being mired in sin that brings ruin and physical death, regardless of your faith in Christ.

If anything you're chastised even more so as a child of God.

So while it is well and good to point out the sins of the father, that we may learn from them and not do them, we can't blame our troubles on God punishing us for our father's sake. It's entirely up to us to forge ahead in a righteous life.

teachings.title: The Lord met him and sought to kill him
teachings.summary: Moses' uncircumcised son shows that letting unsaved or carnal family hold us back from God's will makes us lukewarm and brings God's chastening.
teachings.text:
*And it came to pass by the way in the inn, that the Lord met him, and sought to kill him.*

That escalated quickly!

Moses sought to return to Egypt to lead the people out of captivity with the word of God that they may believe and signs and wonders that they may know, but his own son he had not brought into the covenant of Abraham.

Zipporah cuts the foreskin off their son and casts it at Moses' feet. Angry that she had to tend to this bloody business, maybe even angry that she was being uprooted to go with him back to Egypt. Maybe their son wasn't circumcised because she opposed it, and backslidden Moses went along to avoid this kind of confrontation with his wife.

That's the application I take from it, the final excuse many of us have against doing God's will for us is the anger and confrontation we will have with loved ones. The division of family Jesus warned about in the gospels. But it is clear Zipporah isn't happy about any of it.

We may be similarly hindered in our Christian walk by loved ones and relatives who aren't where we are spiritually. Who may be unsaved or have the cares of the world in their hearts. Who put the carnality of life before serving God. And at some point, God will seek our lives for being castaway, for putting their objections over God's will. For our being half in and half out. Lukewarm.

teachings.title: Faith expected to grow
teachings.summary: After salvation our faith should grow by believing a preserved Bible and its doctrine, avoiding the snares of false teachers and carnal readings of scripture.
teachings.text:
Once you believe on the gospel and have faith that it's true, that Jesus died for your sins and that you have eternal life that can never be lost or taken away from you because of His perfect work on the cross, your faith is expected to grow.

We are conformed into the vessel that God needs for His purpose. In order to do that, you have to believe that you can find the will of God. You have to have faith that His word is available to us that we may know His will. You have to have a Bible that contains the whole word that you believe is inspired and preserved. You have to believe the doctrine that His will reveals to us through the Holy Spirit. You have to have faith that it's not by your works of righteousness but by those He has elected us too do. By His will not ours.

There are many stumbling blocks and snares laid in our path as we run towards the finish that we are predestinated for. They are laid there by people who either are not saved and fumbling, or are vipers who are deliberately misleading. You miss out on so much of God's word and the joy of living faith to faith. Contending for the faith set before us.

We've all been sidetracked off of the path by doctrines of devils and doubtful disputations at one point or another. Getting caught up in the worldly aspects that people draw out of scripture, taking things in a carnal way like Nicodemus.

In that we lose track of the spiritual aspects. Which, when we have faith in them, transforms us here in this world that we may better serve him and His will, for His glory in the next.

teachings.title: Moses' face shone
teachings.summary: Time with the Lord changed Moses so His glory shone, and Christians who walk in the Spirit reflect God's glory and must not hide their light though the world hates it.
teachings.text:
And so we see, after 40 days upon the mount with the Lord, Moses having fasted and prayed and recording all God commanded, he returns to the people and his face shown in the reflected glory of God, so much so that the sinful people couldn't stand to look upon Moses.

We know that here the veil was placed upon them that they may not look upon the glory of the Lord, but in Christ Jesus we may boldly go before God, the veil torn in twain. Removed that we may see Him in His word.

We see in Moses that his spending time with the Lord changed him, and the glory of God shone through him.

We who are saved Christians who walk in the Spirit, reading His word, praying ceaselessly, spreading the Gospel to others, feeding the new man, we are similarly changed. We have the same glory, magnified and reflected in us, shining as a light unto the world.

And sinful man can't bear to look at us. They get angry. Resentful. They call for a veil to cover our faith. And sadly, many Christians today hide our light behind a bushel.

But Jesus said to let our light shine.

*Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.*

teachings.title: Not what is in it for me
teachings.summary: Christians should stop doing the bare minimum and instead serve God gladly in every part of life, because it pleases Him.
teachings.text:
We Christians often approach the Bible with a "what is in it for me" attitude. From our salvation to our sanctification, to our separation. And mostly to our sin and compromise and rationalizing. Of doing the bare minimum in every thing, because we have to. Not with joy in service of the Lord God.

We dread work, family obligations, being hospitable and neighborly. Avoiding commitments and shirking responsibilities, and rationalize it with our "works," we pray, we go to church, we read the Bible, we share the Gospel. We do that which is expected to varying degrees and with minimal enthusiasm, not to please God but to be seen of men, to justify being slack in other areas of life.

Instead we should submit to serving God in everything. Who is holy and Whose glory we cannot see without falling down in repentance and fear and trembling, worshiping Him. As the angels in Heaven do without ceasing, we should serve God upon His throne, as glad servants to Him. In everything we do. For He is Holy, so we should be holy.

Because it is pleasing to God.

teachings.title: Our sanctification is not about salvation
teachings.summary: Walking in the Spirit reveals more sin and gives grace to escape it, a refining that makes us useful vessels, not a means of salvation.
teachings.text:
And, if we walk in the spirit we will also learn more about the holiness of God and His law, and in that knowledge come to see more things that are sinful. It is impossible to feed the new man with the things of God and not come to be convicted by the Spirit that things we thought not sin, actually are. But the great mystery of that dichotomy is that, despite the knowledge increasing our occasion for the flesh, we have the grace and power to escape from it.

**1 Corinthians 10:13**
*There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.*

It is a refining process. One that removes thorns in our flesh we didn't know we had. This process of sanctification makes us more valuable vessels for God's will. It makes us better able to serve His Gospel. To have real fruits of the spirit. To win others to Christ, and further, to instruct and guide babes in Christ to maturity that they may be able to better serve God as well.

This is the point of our Christian walk.

It's not about you. It's not about finding yourself, or happiness or whatever new age and pagan selfish nonsense our flesh comes up with to lead us away from the spirit.

We are saved already, and justified by the perfect work of Christ Jesus that we believe on. Rejoice. In His blood we have overcome.

Our sanctification isn't about salvation. It is about becoming acceptable tools in God's shed. To be workmen who aren't ashamed. Good and faithful servants.

teachings.title: Present your bodies a living sacrifice
teachings.summary: Doctrine must be applied by presenting ourselves holy in service, not conformed to the world, each using his gifts to edify the one body.
teachings.text:
Having established all things, Paul now begins the practical application of the doctrines he has laid out. My favorite sermons are those that really tear into the meat of the word and then give practical application, how that doctrine can change your life and make you more able to work for God.

Knowledge and wisdom.

It isn't enough to know the word or have understanding of how it all connects, without taking the implications and applying it to our lives. How to be doers of the word and not hearers only.

Paul, in the letter to the Romans, lays out some heavy doctrine in dense language, the revelation of God, the reprobate doctrine, salvation by grace through faith alone, to the Greek and Jew alike, the understanding of God's grace and the purpose of our salvation. And the understanding of a spiritual Israel, not of the flesh.

But what then?

Chapter 12, in clear and concise language tells us.

That we present our bodies as a loving sacrifice, without blemish, which is our service, separated to the Gospel. Be holy that we may be better able to be of service to God. Vessels fitted for glory. Blameless.

This isn't an appeal to hit the gym and not eat poorly. Our bodies are corruptible, and flesh is going to lead us to sin. It is about walking in the spirit that we may not fulfil the lusts of that flesh, and by example bring others to Christ.

He writes, *be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind*, which comes from walking in the spirit. To know the will of God. Proving, testing to see what is acceptable.

We are to remain humble, understanding that to every man of faith God has shaped to a purpose. Not all have the same gifts, the same talents, but all are members of the same body, which is Christ. None more important or less important. A similar theme Found in **1 Corinthians 12**:

*But now are they many members, yet but one body. And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.*

And so each of us should seek to use the talents we have to edify the whole of the body of believers.

*Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching; Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.*

So, to our measure, we all make perfect the will of God. And we see too, that attitude is everything.

teachings.title: Let love be without dissimulation
teachings.summary: True love is honest and must hate evil, so the world's tolerant, manipulative love and the sodomites' love is love slogan are evil called good.
teachings.text:
*Let love be without dissimulation. Abhor that which is evil; cleave to that which is good.*

Dissimulation is deceit, dishonesty regarding intent. Concealing motives. Love without dissimilation requires also to abhor, to hate, that which is evil.

Speaking the truth in love. There is no love in manipulation or in hidden agendas. There is no love without hate.

These two tendencies of the world, to see all relationships as transactional, and so what men call love is often manipulative and controlling. Toxic. And with this toxic false love comes the lack of judgment, calling nothing evil. Tolerating all manner of corruption and perversion. "Not judging" but allowing others to do as they will and calling it good.

It is codependency, an allowance for other's sin that we then can remain in our own. This isn't love.

God's love is without manipulation. It is freely given. We don't have to work for it. Unconditional. To avail ourselves of it, we have to believe He so loved us He gave His only begotten Son. But His love came first, while we were yet sinners.

And God hates evil. Many falsely say "God is love" and ignore His holy nature and the revelation of wrath against the wicked. His word telling us of abominations to Him. For example:

**Proverbs 6:16-19**
*These six things doth the Lord hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, An heart that deviseth wicked imaginations, feet that be swift in running to mischief, A false witness that speaketh lies, and he that soweth discord among brethren*.

The wicked slogan of the prideful sodomites, "Love is Love," is simply putting evil for good, bitter for sweet.

It is impossible to love without hate.

teachings.title: Rejoicing in hope, patient in tribulation
teachings.summary: Christians should be cheerful in hope, patient in trouble and constant in prayer, as Paul and Silas singing in prison won the Philippian jailer.
teachings.text:
*Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer.*

Be cheerful. Not a doomer. You have the hope of Christ, act like it. Not fearful, but let that joy come off of you. It is contagious.

Be patient in tribulation. This applies obviously to the persecution for our faith, in Christ. But it is more than that. Try not to let the petty frustrations of this world get to you, lead you to wrath, being a bad report to the Gospel we live by.

Continuing in prayer, always. Talk to God throughout the day. Give Him thanks and praise. While we shouldn't make a show of prayer, as is the habit of some, we shouldn't be ashamed to ask God's blessings for others and praise for when He answers or blesses.

Think of the Philippian Jailer, who was saved by Paul and Silas, and the church planted there that did great things for the Lord. It all came about because, despite being in chains and captive, they sang hymns and Psalms and cheerfully held themselves out as content even in tribulation.

**Philippians 2:1-5**
*If there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies, Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind. Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves. Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others. Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus*

teachings.title: Kings and priests should not drink wine
teachings.summary: Believers are a royal priesthood and princes, so like the priests and kings they should abstain from alcohol and be sober.
teachings.text:
Note that Moses instructs the priests should remain sober. And that if they drink alcohol and enter into the Tabernacle, they will die.

*Do not drink wine nor strong drink, thou, nor thy sons with thee, when ye go into the tabernacle of the congregation, lest ye die: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations*...

This instruction coming on the heels of the devastating loss of two sons, may have been directed at Aaron in his grief, but it's a standing command from the Lord for those who are called His priests. We who are saved are of the royal priesthood. We are a Tabernacle of the Spirit of God.

Just as **Proverbs 31** states;

*It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; Nor for princes strong drink: Lest they drink, and forget the law, And pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.*

We who are saved are joint heirs to the kingdom. We are princes.

As priests and princes, we should abstain from intoxicants. We are called to be sober. To refrain from the appearance of evil. To be holy because He is holy.

It is incredibly difficult to read these scriptures and come to the conclusion that it's ok to drink booze.

And it is gravely heretical to claim, as the Romans do, that the priests they appoint should drink alcohol as part of their false sacrifice at the altar they claim is holy. Blasphemously calling it the blood of Christ.

teachings.title: Liberty from sin to walk in the Spirit
teachings.summary: Salvation by grace without works frees believers to be sanctified by the Spirit, which is why faithful Baptist churches bear the fruit of separated lives.
teachings.text:
This is the practical application of the law, and the spiritual application for those of us at liberty from sin in Christ, we see the pattern of what is right in God's eyes, that we may be sanctified by Him through the Spirit.

Because of the weakness of the flesh and the failing of sinful man, we need a savior. We need Christ, and through the grace of God, we are given Jesus to do what we couldn't. That by faith in Him we have remission of sin and peace with God. And in that peace, paid for entirely by the blood of Jesus, we can then be sanctified by the Spirit.

We are to standfast in the liberty wherewith Christ has made us free. Not being entangled again with the yoke of bondage. Our unrighteousness done away with by the grace of God to His glory. His mercy being a revelation from Heaven through we who are saved that others may see and come to the knowledge of the truth, and repent towards God. Believing on Christ, to be set at liberty as well.

Despite some, who have crept in privily to spy out liberty, and who slanderously report that we say "let us do evil..." The liberty we have from sin, the blessing that God will not impute sin to us, is to allow us to then walk in the spirit and not fulfill the lusts of the flesh. To strive for the mark that God calls us towards, that we may be conformed to His use, that His will be done. That we be sanctified. That we be holy because He is holy. And in that sanctification, we can bring others to Christ, being a light unto the world as Israel was to be to other nations.

This is why, if we take an honest look at those who preach salvation by grace through faith, without works, without depending on our own selves to turn from sin, or change our lives, or "make Jesus our Lord," but by acknowledging the truth of God, we see so many who are living for God today.

We see those set free in Christ turning from sin, walking in the Spirit, doing great things for the Lord. Not sanctification to gain justification, but sanctification to become vessels fit for His use. That we may be blameless before men. That we may be justified before men, who may say, as in **James 2**, show me your faith by your works. That we may lead others to the truth.

And so, you see independent fundamental Baptist churches that are soul winning, studying to be approved, comparing that which they received with scripture to see if it is so. Engaged in the edification of the local church and reaching out to the poor, the brokenhearted, that they may find peace with God.

Fundamentalist Baptists are often the most separated, actually allowing the Spirit to work effectually in them to remove thorns from their hearts, and to feed the new man, starving the flesh.

This is not to say all Baptists or even a majority of Baptist churches are perfect. This is not to say that just by being Baptist, you become justified or holier than anyone else, or that only a Baptist Church can achieve this.

But the fruit of the more stedfast Baptist churches is undeniably a more separated people doing great works for the Lord.

teachings.title: Let no man judge you in meat or holy days
teachings.summary: Sanctification is not automatic or required for salvation, and believers must not be beguiled by philosophy, traditions or asceticism that pass for holiness.
teachings.text:
I would that all who believe on Christ for salvation come to the understanding that, as befitting a quickened spirit, a new man, we put off the lusts of the flesh and put on the things of God. Mortifying our members, being dead to sin.

But as Paul explains, this isn't automatic. It isn't even a necessity to salvation, as he is writing we who are saved by faith in Christ.

And because it is not automatic, and yet our new man cries out for us to be holy, many men take advantage of this conflict, warning within our members. They come with philosophy and vain deceit; that is the ideas of men that claim to know truth, often that is hidden, that doesn't come from scripture. Or from traditions of men, that things that come from the vain beliefs, and are adopted as religious practices, must be followed. These things aren't of Christ.

Christ in whom we not only have died with and been quickened, and redeemed, our sins done away with and the ordinances taken away. Nailed to His cross.

Therefore, we should not allow any man to judge us in meat, or in drink, or in respect to an holiday, or new moon, or sabbath, all of which were shadows of Christ, or any other condition that they teach for doctrine that are commandments of men and offered in their place.

This means that the vain philosophy of men, as well as the old testament strictures, have no power over we who are saved by faith in Christ. And men who place these things as stumbling blocks and snares are attempting to beguile us. Trapping us into things like voluntary humility, that is sackcloth and ashes. Self-flagellation. Aestheticism, the denial of self for the purpose of self-righteousness (*Touch not; taste not; handle not; Which all are to perish with the using)*.

Weird doctrines like the worship of angels (or saints). Things that they haven't seen themselves, but imagine in their fleshly mind. Things other than Christ who is the head of us who are saved.

Don't be misled by people who indeed seem holy, who may be able to make an argument of men in the wisdom of how they worship in their humility and neglecting things of the body. Unsaved and even reprobates, can fast for example. They may live without gluttony or abstaining from alcohol. They may be even living "cleaner" than some saved Christians. They may refuse to celebrate certain holidays or feasts, citing earthly reasons and the denial of themselves as a form of righteousness. But these are all lies and not of Christ, in whom is liberty.

Chapter 3 goes into details of how a saved Christian *should* seek to clean up their lives. These things that should be done because we are free in Christ and dead to the flesh. Not because man tells us to. Not to show our own holiness but to put off these deeds as new creatures, not beholden to the things of the flesh. But renewed in the knowledge of Christ, as the elect of God. Using the wisdom of His doctrines to teach and rebuke one another. Giving thanks to God through Christ Jesus.

It is the subtle difference between legalism and rejoicing that we are free in grace. And discernment is required.

teachings.title: We are God's servants, bought with a price
teachings.summary: The jubilee reminds us we are God's servants bought by Christ's blood, so we work honestly for others as working for Him and trust Him to provide.
teachings.text:
Ultimately, the ordinances of jubilee serve as a sobering reminder that we are servants of God, and we cannot be given or taken in bondage to any other master.

We may work and toil for another, to pay our way and support our family, but not as slaves, because we are bought for a price already, by the blood of Christ. And so, even as we work here on this earth, we answer to Him. And so, the admonitions in the epistles to be good employees, hard working and honest, because we work for God, is the lived implication of this truth, that we are His.

It reminds us that He provides. That even the ground we must toil to work, the curse of Adam, is His. That bounty or dearth, it is of God. That we can rest in His promise. That when He says we need not work, but that He will give us what we need, we can believe it. It's a constant reminder to the Isralites the thing we as Christians take comfort in, in the Spirit.

teachings.title: Romans 13: living in godly subjection
teachings.summary: Believers are to submit to the authorities God ordains, obeying God rather than man only where they conflict, and trust God, for godly subjection is how God changes who rules over us.
teachings.text:
Romans 13 continues the theme of how saved Christians are to behave. It begins telling us God's view of earthly authority. Parents, bosses, civic leaders, law enforcement, all authorities under God, wicked and cruel or righteous and kind, to serve His will.

Of course we are to follow the higher law of God when earthly authority contradicts it. We are to obey God rather than man, but *if at all possible to live peaceably with all men*.

Many of us bristle at this. It requires our subjection and faith that God will protect and deliver us. Paying custom and tribute to people we know are wicked, stupid, foolish, deceitful is a hard thing to swallow. Not going into reactionary spirals. Not acting from fear. Honoring God by honoring those he's placed in authority over you. Starting with parents for children, husbands for wives, bosses for husbands.

When authority places you in conflict with God, meekly and in His name refuse, but attempt to offer a solution, even one that may harm your interests short term, that you may render what is acceptable to God and in doing so be rewarded long term.

This is so hard in our current year. But if it's fake and gay, can't be voted out, can't be fed posted, and God is with you anyways, what more can we do but live in Godly subjection? At worse be persecuted for His sake and be rewarded here and for eternity. At best be an example as to how God delivers His sons and daughters from tribulation so that others may believe, and in doing so change the nature of the people, turning them towards God. This is how the Bible teaches us we change who rules over us to a more benevolent or tolerable authority. It's how we win.

Hard lesson in faith.

teachings.title: Ananias and Sapphira: chastened unto death
teachings.summary: Ananias and Sapphira were saved church members, and their deaths show not lost salvation but that God scourges His own children for sin, even unto death.
teachings.text:
Acts 5 picks up immediately following the last verses of 4, where the gathered believers of the assembly had just praised God in Jesus name, and been filled with the Holy Ghost to preach the scriptures boldly. They had all things in common, meaning they shared possessions as needed, forsaking materialism to edify the church and do great things for the Lord. One disciple, Barnabas had just sold property and donated the sum to the church at Jerusalem. Likely to praise and blessings. And so we meet a married couple, Ananias and Sapphira.

Ananias and Sapphira, in the context of seeing Barnabas coveted his praise and honor in the church, and having land themselves to sell, sold it for a sum, but presented to the Apostles a lesser amount, keeping a portion of the proceeds for themselves while saying they gave all of it to the church.

Peter, by the Holy Ghost calls out Ananias, who is present before them presenting the gift. Peter says he knows that it's not the full total, and asks why lie to the Holy Ghost about it considering they weren't required to sell the land at all, or to give any of the money to the church. They had every right to give a portion, as it was theirs to give.

But the lying for praise and to be favored among the congregation is the problem, and confronted, Ananias collapses dead at Peter's feet.

The brothers bury him, and a few hours later, as they are putting him in the ground along comes the wife, Sapphira.

Peter gives her a chance to be truthful, and she sticks to the story her and her husband had concocted. Peter, again in the Spirit curses her to the same fate of her husband, striking her dead. The gathered now know Ananias' death wasn't just happenstance, but that the couple has been punished by God.

Were Ananias and Sapphira saved? Didn't they just feel the presence of the Holy Ghost when the church prayed the chapter before? The Bible says in Acts 4 that the entire church was of one heart and one soul. They were of that church. I think the implication is clear they were.

But their being in Heaven when they die, justified by faith and Jesus' imputed righteousness didn't keep them from sinning, nor did it stop God from punishing them with their lives.

Many of the religion of works, who maintain that you must repent of sinning to be saved, and claim that the Gospel of Christ, salvation by faith in grace, is a "license to sin." And so, being fruit inspectors, take this story as evidence they were not believers. But what it shows is that God chastises His own for our iniquity. He takes the rod to His children when they sin. The Bible says He scourges His adopted sons and daughters. Even unto death.
